## DOMAINS

### Algebra

Groups: 5 · Skills: 16

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Mathematical expressions, equalities, inequalities, variables and unknowns, patterns, generalizations, and symbolic descriptions of relationships. The scope is not constrained to a particular age, numerical range, or notation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Teñdeuler, örnekter, sandardy bıldıretın ärıpter men zañdylyqtar bailanystardy qalai sipattap, belgısız mänderdı tabuğa kömektesetının zertte.

#### Teñdıkter

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/equalities/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Equality as equal values of two expressions, the truth of equalities, and completing missing components.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Teñdık belgısınıñ mağynasyn, matematikalyq tūjyrymdardy tekserudı jäne teñdık dūrys bolatyndai jetıspeitın mändı tabudy üiren.

##### Dūrys teñdıktı tolyqtyru

[completeEquality.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/equalities/completeEquality.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A missing value in an equation must make both sides equal. Finding it requires considering the operation structure and relevant number domain, rather than filling a familiar fact without checking.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Teñdıktıñ ekı jağyndağy män bırdei bolatyndai jetıspeitın sandy taba alasyñ.

##### Teñdık belgısınıñ mağynasyn tüsınu

[equalityMeaning.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/equalities/equalityMeaning.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The equality sign asserts equal values on both sides, not a prompt to compute an answer. Either side may contain numbers, expressions, or other mathematical objects; equality is determined by their values.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Teñdık belgısı ekı jaqtağy örnekterdıñ mänı bırdei ekenın bıldıredı, tek odan keiın jauap jazylady degen söz emes.

##### Sandyq teñdıkter men teñsızdıkterdı tekseru

[trueFalseEquality.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/equalities/trueFalseEquality.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** An equality is true when both sides have the same value; an inequality is true when the specified order relation holds. Merely performing an operation on one side does not make a statement true.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı jaqtağy mänderdı salystyryp, teñdık ne teñsızdık dūrys ekenın teksere alasyñ.

#### Örnekter

Skills: 4

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/expressions/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The meanings of mathematical expressions involving operations, parentheses, and variables, including correct order of operations.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Örnekterdı oqudy, jaqşa men amaldardyñ oryndalu retın qoldanudy jäne ärıp sandy bıldırgende mänın esepteudı üiren.

##### Amaldar retın qoldanu

[orderOfOperations.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/expressions/orderOfOperations.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** An expression's value follows the agreed order of operations: parentheses, multiplication/division, then addition/subtraction, applying associativity or left-to-right rules where appropriate. Changing the order can change the result.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Örnektıñ mänın aldymen jaqşa ışındegı amaldardy, sodan keiın köbeitu men böludı, soñynda qosu men azaitudy oryndap taba alasyñ.

##### Jaqşalary bar örnekterdı esepteu

[parentheses.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/expressions/parentheses.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Parentheses specify how subexpressions are grouped and can change the conventional order of operations. Evaluation must respect nesting and operation precedence without arbitrarily moving or removing parentheses.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jaqşa ışındegı bölıkterdı aldymen eseptep, tıptı jaqşalardyñ ışınde tağy jaqşa bolsa da, örnektıñ mänın taba alasyñ.

##### Sandyq örnekterdı oqu jäne jazu

[readNumericExpressions.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/expressions/readNumericExpressions.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A numerical expression defines a value using numbers, arithmetic operations, and possibly parentheses. Interpreting its written structure is distinct from calculating its numerical value.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandar, amal tañbalary jäne jaqşalar arqyly örnekterdı oqyp, jaza alasyñ; olardyñ mänın bırden esepteu mındettı emes.

##### Ainymalysy bar qarapaiym örnekterdıñ mänın tabu

[variableValue.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/expressions/variableValue.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A letter in an expression may represent a variable assigned a value under given conditions. Substituting that value and performing operations evaluates the expression; symbolic notation does not establish a different arithmetic law.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ärıp sandy bıldırse, onyñ ornyna berılgen mändı qoiyp, örnektı eseptei alasyñ.

#### Simvoldyq modeldeu

Skills: 1

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/formalization/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Representing relationships in a short situation using arithmetic or simple algebraic notation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Naqty ne matematikalyq jağdailardyñ mağynasyn saqtap, sandarmen, amal tañbalarymen jäne qarapaiym teñdeulermen körsetudı üiren.

##### Jağdaidy örnekpen nemese teñdeumen körsetu

[translateSituation.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/formalization/translateSituation.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A symbolic model must preserve the essential quantities and dependencies of a real or mathematical situation, including known and unknown roles. Correct numbers combined by the wrong operation do not yield an appropriate model.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jağdaidy belgılı jäne belgısız şamalardy dūrys körsetetın matematikalyq örnekpen nemese teñdeumen beinelei alasyñ.

#### Zañdylyqtar

Skills: 2

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/patterns/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Regular numerical changes following a rule and recognizing a sequence's structure from several terms.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandar zañdylyğyn zerttep, tūraqty özgerıstı anyqta, erejenı tekser jäne tızbektı jalğastyr.

##### Tūraqty qadammen sandyq zañdylyqty jalğastyru

[arithmeticPattern.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/patterns/arithmeticPattern.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A number sequence such as 4, 7, 10, 13 has a constant increment of three; extend it by repeatedly applying the same step to the preceding term.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Är joly bırdei sandy qosyp nemese azaityp, sandar tızbegın jalğastyra alasyñ.

##### Ösetın zañdylyq erejesın tabu

[growingPattern.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/patterns/growingPattern.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** From successive values such as 2, 6, 10, one may infer a growth rule of adding four, but the proposed rule must be tested against all supplied terms before treating it as established.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ösetın sandar tızbegınıñ erejesın tauyp, onyñ berılgen barlyq sandarğa säikes keletının teksere alasyñ.

#### Belgısız mänder

Skills: 6

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/unknowns/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relationships between components and results of the four arithmetic operations that allow an unknown quantity to be found and verified.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tört amaldyñ bailanysyn paidalanyp, belgısız sandardy tabudy jäne tekserudı üiren.

##### Belgısız qosylğyşty tabu

[unknownAddend.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/unknowns/unknownAddend.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Find an unknown addend by subtracting the known addend from the sum in the relevant number domain. Substitution into the original equation verifies the part-whole relationship.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qosyndydan belgılı qosylğyşty azaityp, belgısız qosylğyşty tauyp, qosu arqyly teksere alasyñ.

##### Belgısız bölıngıştı tabu

[unknownDividend.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/unknowns/unknownDividend.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** For exact division, the dividend equals the product of divisor and quotient. Finding an unknown dividend uses the inverse relation with multiplication and is checked against the original equality.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qaldyqsyz bölude bölgıştı bölındıge köbeitıp, belgısız bölıngıştı taba alasyñ.

##### Belgısız bölgıştı tabu

[unknownDivisor.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/unknowns/unknownDivisor.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Given a nonzero dividend and nonzero quotient, determine the divisor by dividing the dividend by the quotient in the relevant number domain. Check that the divisor is nonzero and the original division holds.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bölıngış pen nölden özge bölındı belgılı bolsa, belgısız bölgıştı tauyp, onyñ nöl emes ekenın teksere alasyñ.

##### Belgısız köbeitkıştı tabu

[unknownFactor.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/unknowns/unknownFactor.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Given a product and a known nonzero factor, determine the missing factor by division within the permitted number domain. Verify by reconstructing the original product.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Köbeitındı men nölden özge bır köbeitkış belgılı bolsa, bölu arqyly ekınşısın tauyp, köbeitu arqyly teksere alasyñ.

##### Belgısız azaiğyşty tabu

[unknownMinuend.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/unknowns/unknownMinuend.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** When the minuend is unknown, reconstruct it by adding the subtrahend to the given difference. Verification must satisfy the original equation; this differs from finding an unknown subtrahend.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Azaitudağy belgısız azaiğyşty tabu üşın azaitqyşty aiyrmağa qosa alasyñ.

##### Belgısız azaitqyşty tabu

[unknownSubtrahend.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/algebra/unknowns/unknownSubtrahend.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Given the minuend and difference, find the unknown subtrahend by subtracting the difference from the minuend. Component positions matter: the inverse formulas for unknown minuend and unknown subtrahend are not interchangeable.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Belgısız azaitqyşty tabu üşın azaiğyştan aiyrmany azaita alasyñ.

### Arifmetika

Groups: 5 · Skills: 74

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The meanings and properties of addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division; their relationships; exact and approximate calculation methods; justifications of algorithms; and result verification. The Curriculum determines numerical ranges and degree of formalization.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qosu, azaitu, köbeitu jäne böludıñ özara bailanysyn zerttep, olardy mölşerlerdı esepteuge, şamalauğa jäne nätijenı tekseruge paidalan.

#### Qosu

Skills: 8

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/addition/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Combining quantities, properties of sums, place-value regrouping, and methods for calculating and checking results.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qosudyñ mölşerlerdı qalai bırıktıretının ne arttyratynyn jäne onyñ qasietterı men razriadtyq mänderı qosyndyny eseptep, tekseruge qalai kömektesetının bıl.

##### Qosu — mağynasy men modelderı

[addMeaning.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/addition/addMeaning.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Addition can model the union of disjoint sets or an increase from an initial quantity. The same sum retains its value across scenarios, although the roles of components and the kind of change can differ.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qosudyñ qai kezde bölek mölşerlerdı bırıktıretının, qai kezde bastapqy mölşerdı arttyratynyn ajyratyp, ekı jağdaidy da qosyndy türınde körsete alasyñ.

##### Qosu — nöl

[addZero.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/addition/addZero.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Zero is the additive identity: for any number a, a + 0 = 0 + a = a. Distinguish the absence of a quantity contributed by an addend from the absence of an operation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Nöldı qosqanda san özgermeidı, nöl qosu tañbasynyñ qai jağynda tūrsa da.

##### Qosu — terımdılık qasietı

[associativeAddition.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/addition/associativeAddition.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Associativity of addition allows regrouping three or more addends without changing their sum. Alongside commutativity it supports flexible strategies but does not permit arbitrary changes to addend values.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Üş nemese odan köp sandy qosqanda olardy ärtürlı toptastyrsañ da, qosyndy özgermeidı.

##### Qosu — bağan türınde

[columnAddition.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/addition/columnAddition.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Written column addition aligns operands by place value, adds corresponding positions, and carries complete tens to the next place. Carry marks and the resulting numeral must reflect decimal positional notation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandardy razriadtary boiynşa turalap, bağan türınde qosa alasyñ jäne qajet bolsa, kelesı razriadqa auystyrasyñ.

##### Qosu — auystyrymdylyq qasietı

[commutativeAddition.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/addition/commutativeAddition.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Commutativity of addition states a + b = b + a: exchanging addends preserves their sum. This changes operand order, not operand values, and can be used to choose a convenient computation order.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qosylatyn sandardyñ ornyn auystyrsañ da, qosyndy özgermeidı.

##### Qosu — ondyqtan attap ötu

[crossTenAddition.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/addition/crossTenAddition.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** If the ones sum exceeds nine, ten ones can be exchanged for one ten with remaining ones. This place-value regrouping preserves the numerical value regardless of calculation method.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bırlıkterdıñ qosyndysy onğa nemese odan köpke jetse, on bırlıktı bır ondyqqa auystyruğa bolady; jalpy qosyndy özgermeidı.

##### Qosu — ondyqqa tolyqtyru

[makeTenStrategy.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/addition/makeTenStrategy.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The make-ten strategy decomposes an addend so that a part combines with the other addend to reach a convenient ten; the remainder is then added. Regrouping preserves the original sum by addition properties.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır qosylğyşty bölıkterge ajyratyp, aldymen kelesı tolyq ondyqqa jetıp, sodan keiın qalğanyn qosa alasyñ; qosyndy özgermeidı.

##### Razriadtardy auystyryp qosu

[regrouping.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/addition/regrouping.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Addition with place-value regrouping exchanges ten units of one place for one unit of the next place (ones to tens, tens to hundreds). The same principle applies regardless of how many digits the addends have; single or multiple carries preserve the total sum.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qosu kezınde qajet bolsa, on bırlıktı bır ondyqqa nemese on ondyqty bır jüzdıkke auystyra alasyñ.

#### Qosu men azaitudy bırıktıru

Skills: 13

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The relationship between inverse addition and subtraction, part-whole relationships, and flexible methods for mental calculation and self-checking.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qosu men azaitudyñ bölıkterdı bütınmen qalai bailanystyratynyn bıl jäne eseptep, tekseru üşın razriadtyq mänderdı, juyqtaudy ärı kerı amaldardy paidalan.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — tolyq ondyqtar

[addSubtractTens.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/addSubtractTens.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiples of ten can be added or subtracted as quantities of the corresponding place-value unit. Ordinary operation properties still apply, but the decimal place weight must be preserved.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tolyq ondyqtardy olardyñ sanyn esepteu arqyly qosyp ne azaityp, razriadtyq mänın saqtai alasyñ.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — kerı amaldarmen tekseru

[checkWithInverse.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/checkWithInverse.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The result of 63 - 28 can be checked by adding 28 back to the computed difference. A disagreement indicates an error and illustrates inverse operations as a verification method.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qosudy azaitumen, al azaitudy qosumen tekserıp, kerı amal arqyly qatelerdı taba alasyñ.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — kompensatsiia ädısı

[compensation.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/compensation.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compensation adjusts one operand to simplify mental calculation and then offsets that change to preserve the result. For 39 + 8, compute 40 + 8 = 48 and subtract the extra one.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qosu ne azaitudy jeñıldetu üşın bır sandy özgertıp, keiın sol özgerıstı ötep, dūrys nätijenı saqtai alasyñ.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — nätijenı bağalau

[estimateResult.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/estimateResult.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Place-value reasoning, rounding, or bounds provide an estimated order of magnitude for a result. Such estimates can reveal large errors but cannot independently establish an exact answer.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandardy döñgelektep nemese razriadtyq mänge süienıp, qosyndyny ne aiyrmany şamalap, tym alşaq jauaptardy baiqai alasyñ.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — 10 kölemındegı negızgı amaldar

[factsWithin10.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/factsWithin10.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Addition and subtraction facts can be recalled or derived without recounting physical objects. Part-whole relations and inverse operations support accurate computation and generalization.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Är närsenı bır-bırlep sanamai, sandardyñ bailanysy arqyly on kölemındegı qosyndy men aiyrmany taba alasyñ.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — 20 kölemındegı negızgı amaldar

[factsWithin20.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/factsWithin20.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Fluency within twenty combines knowledge of fundamental number facts with deriving sums and differences using decomposition, complements, decimal structure, and inverse operations. Speed alone does not establish correctness.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Belgılı esepteu faktılerın, sandardy jıkteudı jäne qosu men azaitu bailanysyn paidalanyp, jiyrma kölemındegı qosyndy men aiyrmany taba alasyñ.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — jüzdıkter men ondyqtar

[hundredsAndTens.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/hundredsAndTens.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiples of a hundred and ten are calculated as quantities of their corresponding place-value units. Mixed-place computations require equivalent exchanges to preserve overall value.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ondyqtar men jüzdıkterdı razriadtyq mänıne qarai qosyp, azaityp, qajet bolsa qaita toptastyra alasyñ.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — kerı amaldar

[inverseOperations.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/inverseOperations.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Addition and subtraction are inverses in the relevant number domains. For a + b = c, checking c - b = a or c - a = b uses the same mathematical relationship.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandar arasyndağy bailanysty paidalanyp, qosudy azaitumen, azaitudy qosumen kerı qaitara alasyñ.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — 10 sanynyñ qūramy

[numberBonds10.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/numberBonds10.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Ten can be decomposed into multiple ordered or unordered pairs of nonnegative addends whose sum is ten. Increasing one part determines a corresponding decrease in the other while the whole stays fixed.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qosyndysy on bolatyn ärtürlı san jūptaryn tauyp, bır bölık özgerse, ekınşısı qalai özgeretının tüsıne alasyñ.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — bölık pen bütınnıñ bailanysy

[partWhole.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/partWhole.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The additive part-whole model relates a whole to the sum of its components and permits finding an unknown component from the whole and known parts. Do not confuse the whole's total with a component's amount.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bölıkterı boiynşa bütındı nemese bütın men özge bölıkter belgılı bolsa, jetıspeitın bölıktı taba alasyñ.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — razriad boiynşa auyzşa esepteu

[placeValueMental.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/placeValueMental.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Mental place-value decomposition replaces an expression by equivalent calculations on tens and ones. Each step must preserve the sum or difference and be justified by operation properties.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandardy ondyqtar men bırlıkterge jıktep, qosyndyny ne aiyrmany özgertpei oişa qosyp, azaita alasyñ.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — üş tañbaly sandar qaita toptastyrusyz

[threeDigitNoRegroup.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/threeDigitNoRegroup.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Where no carrying or borrowing is required, corresponding hundreds, tens, and ones can be computed separately. Combining the place values produces the same sum or difference.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qaita toptastyru qajet bolmağanda üş tañbaly sandardyñ jüzdıkterın, ondyqtaryn jäne bırlıkterın bölek eseptep qosa nemese azaita alasyñ.

##### Qosu jäne azaitu — ekı tañbaly sandar qaita toptastyrusyz

[twoDigitNoRegroup.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/additionSubtraction/twoDigitNoRegroup.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Without a place-value exchange, tens and ones can be computed separately and their values recombined. This is a special case of general positional arithmetic rather than a different operation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qaita toptastyru qajet bolmağanda ekı tañbaly sandardyñ ondyqtary men bırlıkterın bölek eseptep qosa nemese azaita alasyñ.

#### Bölu

Skills: 23

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Quotients as equal sharing or finding the number of equal groups, basic division facts, remainders, limitations, and verification of division.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Mölşerlerdı teñ bölısudı nemese bütınge qanşa bırdei top syiatynyn anyqtaudy üirenıp, bölındı men qaldyqty köbeitu arqyly tekser.

##### Bölu — ÷ 1 · a ÷ a

[by1AndSelf.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/by1AndSelf.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Dividing any nonzero number by one leaves it unchanged, and a nonzero number divided by itself equals one. These follow from multiplication and do not define 0/0.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandy bırge bölgende ol özgermeidı. Nölden özge kez kelgen sandy özıne bölseñ, bır şyğady.

##### Bölu — ÷ 2

[by2.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/by2.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Division facts by two rely on inverse multiplication-by-two facts and models of halving or pairing. Context determines whether the quotient represents a group count or the size of each group.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekıge bölıp, ekı teñ bölıktı nemese bütındegı ekıden tūratyn toptardyñ sanyn taba alasyñ.

##### Bölu — ÷ 3

[by3.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/by3.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Division facts by three correspond to multiples of three and the inverse of multiplication by three. Derive the quotient from the appropriate product while preserving the chosen sharing or grouping interpretation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Üşke böludı bırdei toptar men üşke köbeitudıñ belgılı nätijelerı arqyly oryndai alasyñ.

##### Bölu — ÷ 4

[by4.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/by4.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Division by four uses inverse multiplication-by-four facts and equal groups of four. Halving twice may yield a quotient but is a possible strategy rather than the definition of the competency.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Törtke böludı bırdei toptar nemese köbeitu nätijelerı arqyly, keide ekı ret jartylau arqyly oryndai alasyñ.

##### Bölu — ÷ 5

[by5.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/by5.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Division by five can be established through multiples of five and inverse multiplication facts. Whether five denotes the group size or group count is determined by context.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Beske böludı bırdei toptar men bestıñ belgılı eselıkterı arqyly oryndai alasyñ.

##### Bölu — ÷ 6

[by6.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/by6.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Division by six is linked to corresponding multiplication-by-six facts. Find the quotient from a known product or an equivalent grouping without restricting competence to one example.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Altyğa böludı bırdei toptar nemese köbeitu nätijelerı arqyly oryndap, bölındını taba alasyñ.

##### Bölu — ÷ 7

[by7.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/by7.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Division by seven draws on multiples of seven and inverse multiplication facts. The relevant quotient is the value that reproduces the dividend when multiplied by seven.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jetıge böludı jetıden tūratyn toptar jäne belgılı köbeitu nätijelerı arqyly oryndap, bölındını taba alasyñ.

##### Bölu — ÷ 8

[by8.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/by8.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Divide by eight using the corresponding multiplication-by-eight fact or a model of equal groups. Apply the relationship to different division facts, not only a single memorized example.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Segızge böludı bırdei toptar nemese segızge bailanysty belgılı köbeitındıler arqyly oryndai alasyñ.

##### Bölu — ÷ 9

[by9.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/by9.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Division by nine is inverse to the matching products with factor nine. Known multiples or equivalent decompositions can determine the quotient across the family of facts.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Toğyzğa böludı toğyzdyñ eselıkterı men köbeitu-bölu bailanysy arqyly oryndai alasyñ.

##### Bölu — nätijenı tekseru

[checkQuotient.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/checkQuotient.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Verify quotient and remainder using a = bq + r together with 0 <= r < b for positive b. The equation alone does not establish the correctness of canonical integer division.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bölgıştı bölındıge köbeitıp, qaldyqty qosu arqyly böludı teksere alasyñ. Qaldyq oñ bölgışten kışı boluy tiıs.

##### Bölu — jartylau jäne ekı eseleu

[doubleHalf.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/doubleHalf.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Half of an even quantity is one of two equal addends composing the whole. Doubling the half restores the original whole and provides an inverse check.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jūp mölşerdı ekı teñ bölıkke bölıp, bıreuın ekı eseleu arqyly teksere alasyñ.

##### Bölu — teñ toptarğa bölu

[equalGrouping.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/equalGrouping.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Quotitive division determines how many groups of a specified size can be formed from a total. When division is not exact, distinguish complete groups from the remainder.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bütınnen belgılı ölşemdegı qanşa tolyq top şyğatynyn jäne qanşa qalatynyn anyqtai alasyñ.

##### Bölu — teñ ülesterge bölu

[equalSharing.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/equalSharing.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Partitive division determines the size of each group from the total and the number of equal groups. Nonzero remainders and integer divisibility may require explicit qualification of the mathematical model.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bütındı sany belgılı teñ toptarğa bölıp, är topqa qanşadan tietının taba alasyñ.

##### Bölu — nölge bölu

[noDivisionByZero.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/noDivisionByZero.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** For nonzero a, 0 × x = a has no solution; for a = 0 it has many, so division by zero cannot define a unique inverse of multiplication. This covers a zero as well as a nonzero dividend.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Nölge böluge bolmaidy: bölınetın san nöl bolsa da, bırmändı anyqtalğan bölındı bolmaidy.

##### Bölu — örnekterdı oqu

[readExpression.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/readExpression.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The dividend represents the total, the nonzero divisor is the second operand, and the quotient is the result. In equal sharing the divisor can specify the number of groups, whereas in grouping it specifies each group's size.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bölu örnegındegı bölıngıştı, bölgıştı jäne bölındını anyqtap, olardy teñ bölısu men toptastyruda tüsıne alasyñ.

##### Bölu — kerı amaldar

[relationToMultiplication.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/relationToMultiplication.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Division is inverse to multiplication: knowing a product and a nonzero factor makes it possible to determine the other factor. This relationship supports checking a quotient by multiplication.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Köbeitu men bölu kerı amaldar bolğandyqtan, köbeitu arqyly bölındını tauyp nemese teksere alasyñ.

##### Bölu — qaldyq bölgışten kışı

[remainderLessDivisor.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/remainderLessDivisor.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** For a positive divisor b, the canonical nonnegative remainder satisfies 0 <= r < b. A remainder at least as large as the divisor means another complete group is still possible.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bütın sandardy oñ sanğa bölgende qaldyq terıs emes jäne bölgışten kışı boluy tiıs.

##### Bölu — tolyq jüzdıkter

[roundHundreds.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/roundHundreds.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Divide multiples of a hundred by one-digit numbers by grouping hundreds and, when needed, exchanging them for tens or ones. The result must satisfy the inverse relation between dividend, divisor, and quotient.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tolyq jüzdıkterdı bır tañbaly sanğa bölıp, qajet bolsa jüzdıkterdı ondyqtarğa nemese bırlıkterge auystyra alasyñ.

##### Bölu — tolyq ondyqtar

[roundTens.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/roundTens.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Division of multiples of ten can operate on whole tens when quotients preserve place-value weights. If the tens do not divide evenly, regroup into smaller units rather than silently discard a remainder.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tolyq ondyqtardy bır tañbaly sanğa bölıp, ondyqtar däl bölınbese, olardy kışırek razriadtyq bırlıkterge auystyra alasyñ.

##### Bölu — üş tañbaly sandy bır tañbaly sanğa

[threeDigitByOne.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/threeDigitByOne.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Decomposing a three-digit dividend into convenient place-value or additive parts allows computing partial quotients and reconstructing the total. Each division must be valid and retain the corresponding place-value weight.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Üş tañbaly sandy bır tañbalyğa yñğaily bölıkterge jıktep, olardyñ bölındılerın qosu arqyly böle alasyñ.

##### Bölu — ekı tañbaly sandy bır tañbaly sanğa

[twoDigitByOne.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/twoDigitByOne.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A dividend may be decomposed into convenient parts that are separately divisible in the chosen number domain, then the partial quotients combined using division's distributivity over a sum. Not every arbitrary partition divides evenly.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı tañbaly sandy bır tañbalyğa oñai bölınetın bölıkterge jıktep, nätijelerın bırıktıre alasyñ.

##### Bölu — qaldyqpen

[withRemainder.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/withRemainder.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Integer division with positive divisor b yields quotient q and remainder r satisfying a = bq + r and 0 <= r < b. The quotient counts complete groups and the remainder is what cannot make another full group.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Oñ bölgışten kışı qaldyğy bar bütın bölındını taba alasyñ; bölgış × bölındı + qaldyq bölıngışke teñ.

##### Bölu — bölıngış nöl

[zeroDividend.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/divide/zeroDividend.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Zero divided by a nonzero number is zero, because that divisor multiplied by zero gives zero. Distinguish a zero dividend from the undefined operation of division by zero.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Nöldı kez kelgen nölden özge sanğa bölseñ, nöl şyğady; būl nölge bölu emes.

#### Köbeitu

Skills: 24

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Products as equal groups or rectangular arrays, multiplication facts and properties, and place-value-based computation methods.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Köbeitudı bırdei toptar men qatar-bağan türındegı ornalasu arqyly zertte, onyñ qasietterı men razriadtyq mänderdı ülken köbeitındılerdı esepteuge paidalan.

##### Köbeitu — tıkbūryşty qatarlar men bağandar modelı

[arrayModel.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/arrayModel.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A rectangular array with the same number of elements in each row models the product of row count and elements per row. Interchanging row and column roles preserves cardinality and demonstrates multiplication commutativity.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Zattardy bırdei qatarlar men bağandarğa ornalastyryp, köbeitudı körsetıp, jalpy sanyn taba alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — terımdılık qasietı

[associative.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/associative.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplication is associative: (ab)c = a(bc). Regrouping factors preserves the product; the law does not permit arbitrary changes to factor values or replacing multiplication with addition.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Üş nemese odan köp sandy köbeitkende köbeitkışterdı ärtürlı toptastyrsañ da, köbeitındı özgermeidı.

##### Köbeitu — × 0 · × 1

[by0And1.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/by0And1.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Zero is absorbing and one is the identity for multiplication: a × 0 = 0 and a × 1 = a in the relevant number domain. These properties do not depend on a concrete object model.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Kez kelgen sandy nölge köbeitseñ nöl şyğady, bırge köbeitseñ san özgermeidı.

##### Köbeitu — × 10

[by10.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/by10.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplying by ten scales a number by a factor of ten. In decimal positional notation each place-value unit shifts to the next higher place; for natural numbers the product has zero in the ones place.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Razriadtyq män arqyly onğa köbeite alasyñ: är razriadtyñ mänı on ese artady.

##### Köbeitu — × 2

[by2.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/by2.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplication by two is doubling: a × 2 = a + a. Equal groups and repeated addition support understanding without making any single representation mandatory.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Mölşerdı özıne qosyp, onyñ ekı esesın taba alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — × 3

[by3.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/by3.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplication facts with factor three concern equal groups of three and successive multiples of three. The products can be derived using operation properties or neighboring known facts rather than memorized in isolation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Üşke köbeitudı üş bırdei top retınde tüsınıp, belgılı nätijeler arqyly üştıñ eselıkterın taba alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — × 4

[by4.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/by4.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplication facts with factor four correspond to four equal groups and can use doubling a doubled amount or other known multiples. A model must distinguish group count from group size.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Törtke köbeitudı tört bırdei top arqyly nemese mölşerdı ekı ret ekı eseleu arqyly oryndai alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — × 5

[by5.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/by5.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Products with factor five relate to successive multiples of five and equal groups. They may be found by repeated addition or decomposition into familiar facts while preserving equal group size.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Beske köbeitudı bes bırdei toppen nemese būrynnan belgılı qosyndylarğa süienıp oryndai alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — × 6

[by6.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/by6.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplication facts with factor six give multiples of six and may be derived from known multiples of five plus one more equal group or other equivalent decompositions. Strategy does not change product identity.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Altyğa köbeitu üşın bes bırdei topqa tağy bıreuın qosa alasyñ nemese belgılı köbeitındılerdı paidalanasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — × 7

[by7.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/by7.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Products with factor seven belong to the family of multiples of seven, connected with equal groups and multiplication properties. Unknown facts can be deduced from neighboring known products.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jetı bırdei top arqyly jetıge köbeitıp, belgısız köbeitındını jaqyn belgılı nätijelerden şyğara alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — × 8

[by8.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/by8.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplication by eight connects equal groups of eight with their total; doubling, decomposition, and known products provide equivalent computation strategies. The family of facts is distinct from a method of learning it.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Segızge köbeitudı segız bırdei top, ekı eseleu nemese eseptı jeñıl bölıkterge jıkteu arqyly oryndai alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — × 9

[by9.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/by9.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiples of nine can be computed from nine equal groups or the relation 9a = 10a - a. Different valid strategies produce the same product without prescribing a single procedure.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Toğyzğa köbeitudı toğyz bırdei toppen nemese onğa köbeitıp, bır topty azaitu arqyly oryndai alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — nätijenı tekseru

[checkProduct.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/checkProduct.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** An estimate indicates the expected order of magnitude of a product; exactness can be checked by a valid inverse operation or independent calculation. Merely reversing factor order may repeat an earlier error rather than check independently.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Köbeitındınıñ şamasyn bağalap, bölu nemese basqa täuelsız esepteu arqyly nätijenı teksere alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — auystyrymdylyq qasietı

[commutative.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/commutative.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplication is commutative: a × b = b × a. Reorienting a rectangular array or establishing another one-to-one mapping can show why exchanging factors does not change the product.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Köbeitkışterdıñ ornyn auystyrsañ da, köbeitındı özgermeidı.

##### Köbeitu — köbeitu nätijelerın şyğaru

[deriveFacts.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/deriveFacts.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** An unknown table product may be derived from familiar products using commutativity, associativity, distributivity, doubling, or changing a factor. This demonstrates structural understanding rather than mere fact recall.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Belgılı köbeitındıler arqyly belgısızderın toptastyrudy özgertıp, sandardy jıktep nemese ekı eselep taba alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — ülestırımdılık qasietı

[distributive.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/distributive.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The distributive law relates a(b + c) to ab + ac. Splitting a factor into convenient addends preserves the product and recombines partial products while maintaining each part's role.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandy bölıkterge bölıp, är bölıktı bırdei köbeitkışke köbeitıp, aralyq köbeitındılerdı qosqanda bastapqy köbeitındını alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — ekı ret eseleu

[doubleTwice.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/doubleTwice.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Four equal groups can be obtained by doubling and then doubling again. This is a calculation strategy for multiplication by four, not necessarily a separate general multiplication concept.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandy ekı eselep, nätijesın qaita ekı eseleu arqyly törtke köbeite alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — teñ toptar

[equalGroups.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/equalGroups.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplication relates the number of equally sized groups, the size of one group, and the total number of objects. Unequal groups cannot be represented by a single group-count-times-group-size product without another model.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bırdei toptardyñ sany men är toptağy zattar sany arqyly jalpy sanyn taba alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — örnekterdı oqu

[readExpression.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/readExpression.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Factors are the inputs to multiplication and the product is its result. In an equal-groups model, factors represent the group count and group size; distinguish this concrete interpretation from the symbolic expression alone.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Köbeitu örnegın oqyp, köbeitkışterı men köbeitındısın anyqtap, ony bırdei toptarmen bailanystyra alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — qaitalanatyn qosu

[repeatedAddition.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/repeatedAddition.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A product of natural factors can be written as repeated addition of equal addends. Reversing this representation requires equality of the addends; an arbitrary sum is not necessarily one repeated-addition product.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bırdei bütın mölşerdı qaitalap qosudy köbeitu türınde körsete alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — tolyq jüzdıkter

[roundHundreds.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/roundHundreds.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A multiple of one hundred represents a count of complete hundreds. Multiplication by a one-digit factor changes that count while respecting the factor of one hundred, not merely manipulating digits.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tolyq jüzdıkterdı bır tañbaly sanğa jüzdıkter sanyn esepteu arqyly köbeite alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — tolyq ondyqtar

[roundTens.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/roundTens.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A multiple of ten can be multiplied by a one-digit factor by multiplying its count of tens and restoring place-value weight. Exchanging tens for hundreds preserves the product.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tolyq ondyqtardy bır tañbaly sanğa köbeitıp, qajet bolsa on ondyqty bır jüzdıkke bırıktıre alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — üş tañbaly sandy bır tañbaly sanğa

[threeDigitByOne.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/threeDigitByOne.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplying a three-digit number by a one-digit factor relies on decomposition into hundreds, tens, and ones and the distributive law. Carrying between places must preserve the total product.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Üş tañbaly sandy bır tañbalyğa jüzdıkter, ondyqtar jäne bırlıkter arqyly köbeitıp, qajet bolsa razriadqa auystyra alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu — ekı tañbaly sandy bır tañbaly sanğa

[twoDigitByOne.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/multiply/twoDigitByOne.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Decompose the two-digit factor into tens and ones, distribute multiplication over the resulting sum, and combine partial products. Each component must retain its original place-value weight.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı tañbaly sandy ondyqtar men bırlıkterge bölıp, är bölıktı bır tañbalyğa köbeitıp, aralyq köbeitındılerdı qosa alasyñ.

#### Azaitu

Skills: 6

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/subtraction/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Removing a part, finding a difference, regrouping place values, and verifying subtraction calculations.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Azaitu qaldyqty, mölşerlerdıñ aiyrmasyn nemese belgısız bölıktı qalai tabuğa kömektesetının jäne razriadtyq mänder esepteu men tekseruge qalai järdemdesetının bıl.

##### Azaitu — bağan türınde

[columnSubtraction.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/subtraction/columnSubtraction.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Written column subtraction aligns like place values and performs needed exchanges before subtracting corresponding digits. Each exchange must correctly affect adjacent places in the decimal system.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandardy razriadtaryna qarai turalap, bağan türınde azaita alasyñ jäne bır razriadta jetkılıksız bolsa, qaita toptastyrasyñ.

##### Azaitu — ondyqtan attap ötu

[crossTenSubtraction.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/subtraction/crossTenSubtraction.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** When the minuend has insufficient ones, exchange one ten for ten ones without changing its value. Crossing ten also admits other equivalent strategies that preserve the difference.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bastapqy sannyñ mänın özgertpei, bır ondyqty on bırlıkke auystyryp, ondyqtan attap azaita alasyñ.

##### Razriadtardy türlendırıp azaitu

[regrouping.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/subtraction/regrouping.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Subtraction with place-value regrouping exchanges a higher-place unit for ten lower-place units when needed, including exchanges across a zero. The same invariant holds for two-digit, three-digit and larger minuends: regrouping changes representation without changing value.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Azaitu kezınde bır razriadtağy bırlıkter jetpese, bır ondyqty on bırlıkke nemese bır jüzdıktı on ondyqqa auystyra alasyñ.

##### Azaitu — mağynasy men modelderı

[subtractMeaning.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/subtraction/subtractMeaning.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Subtraction may model removing a part, finding the difference between two quantities, or finding an unknown component of a known whole. These share an arithmetic relation but differ in known and unknown roles.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Azaitudyñ bölıktı alyp tastau, ekı mölşerdı salystyru nemese belgısız bölıktı tabu ekenın ajyratyp, är jağdaidy azaitu amalymen körsete alasyñ.

##### Azaitu — bırdei san

[subtractSelf.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/subtraction/subtractSelf.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** For every number a, a - a = 0: removing an amount equal to the initial quantity leaves no remainder. This is consistent with the relationship between a number and its additive inverse.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sannan sol sannyñ özın azaitsañ, eşteñe qalmaidy, sondyqtan aiyrma nölge teñ.

##### Azaitu — nöl

[subtractZero.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/arithmetic/subtraction/subtractZero.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Subtracting zero leaves any number unchanged: a - 0 = a. This does not imply that zero minus a positive value is unchanged or that subtraction is commutative.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Nöldı azaitqanda bastapqy san özgermeidı, al azaituda sandardyñ ornyn auystyru — basqa närse.

### Sanau

Groups: 5 · Skills: 15

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The concept of quantity develops through one-to-one correspondence between objects and number words, movement along the natural-number sequence, ordinal positions, and grouping objects for counting.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandar zattardyñ sanyn, rettegı ornyn qalai bıldıretının jäne alğa, artqa ne teñ qadammen qalai sanaudy üiren.

#### Zattardyñ sanyn anyqtau

Skills: 4

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/cardinality/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Understanding number as the cardinality of a set, including the empty set, and methods for determining and comparing the sizes of sets.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jiynda qanşa zat bar ekenın, ol bos bolsa da, anyqta. Zattardyñ ölşemı men ornalasuyn emes, sanyn salystyr.

##### Jiyndağy zattardyñ sanyn anyqtau

[basicCardinality.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/cardinality/basicCardinality.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The final number word in a one-to-one count states the cardinality of the entire set. Neither object arrangement nor counting order changes that cardinality.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Är zatty bır ret qana sana. Soñğy aitylğan san jalpy mölşerdı körsetedı; sanau retı ne ornalasuy özgerse de, ol özgermeidı.

##### Jiyndardy säikestendıru nemese sanau arqyly salystyru

[compareSets.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/cardinality/compareSets.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare set cardinalities through one-to-one matching or by counting each set. Object size, shape, and spatial position do not determine which set has more members.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Zattardy bır-bırden säikestendırıp nemese sanap, qai jiynda köp, az ne bırdei zat baryn tap. Zattardyñ kölemı sanyn anyqtamaidy.

##### Zattardy ondyqtarmen nemese jüzdıktermen sanau

[groupAndCount.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/cardinality/groupAndCount.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine a large set's cardinality by forming complete groups of ten or one hundred and recording any incomplete group separately. The total is the sum of all grouped and ungrouped elements.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Zattardy ondyqtan ne jüzdıkten toptap, qalğanyn qosyp, jalpy sanyn tap.

##### Nöldı bos jiyndağy elementter sany retınde tüsınu

[zero.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/cardinality/zero.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Zero is the cardinality of a set without elements; a container with nothing inside is not itself absent. Zero is a number that participates in the number sequence and arithmetic.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Nöl jiynda eşbır zat joq ekenın bıldıredı. Bos qorap bärıbır bar, al nöl de san bolyp sanalady.

#### Rettık sanau

Skills: 1

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/ordinal/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The distinction between an element's position in an ordered sequence and the total number of elements, separating 'which position?' from 'how many?'.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Zattyñ tañdalğan rettegı ornyn ait, mysaly bırınşı nemese törtınşı. Oryn zattardyñ jalpy sanynan bölek.

##### Rettık oryndy tanu

[basicOrdinal.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/ordinal/basicOrdinal.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** An ordinal number gives an object's position in an ordered sequence relative to a specified direction. It does not give the set's cardinality: changing the order can change positions without changing the total.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Belgılı bağyt boiynşa zattyñ ornyn tap, mysaly sol jaqtan üşınşı. Ret özgerse, oryn özgeruı mümkın, al jalpy san özgermeidı.

#### Jūp jäne taq sandar

Skills: 1

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/parity/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Classifying natural numbers by whether a corresponding collection can be divided into pairs with no remainder.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jūp qūryp, jūp jäne taq sandardy ajyrat. Jūp san bolsa eşteñe qalmaidy, taq bolsa bır zat qalady.

##### Jūptau arqyly jūp jäne taq sandardy anyqtau

[evenOdd.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/parity/evenOdd.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** An even number of objects can be divided into disjoint pairs with none left over; an odd number leaves one. This criterion for integer parity is independent of object arrangement or appearance.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Zattardy jūptastyryp, sannyñ jūp ne taq ekenın tekser. Jūp sannan qaldyq qalmaidy, taq sannan bır zat qalady.

#### Sandar tızbegı

Skills: 5

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/sequence/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Naming consecutive natural numbers, moving forward and backward, and restoring missing elements of the sequence without necessarily starting from one.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ärtürlı sannan bastap, tızbektes sandar boiymen alğa ne artqa jyljy. Ondyq pen jüzdık şekarasynan ötseñ de, kelesı ne jetıspeitın sandy tap.

##### 20 kölemınde kerı sanau

[backward20.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/sequence/backward20.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Find successive predecessors by subtracting one from any starting number. Backward counting must work across ten boundaries, not merely reproduce a memorized counting rhyme.

**User-friendly description (kk):** 20 kölemındegı kez kelgen sannan bastap, bır-bırden kemıtıp kerı sana, ondyqtan ötkende de.

##### 100 kölemınde tura jäne kerı sanau

[forward100.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/sequence/forward100.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Move forward or backward by one from any point within the hundred range. Crossing a ten boundary preserves the succession of neighboring numbers without restarting from one.

**User-friendly description (kk):** 100 kölemındegı kez kelgen sannan bır-bırden alğa ne artqa jyljy, ondyq şekarasynan ötkende de.

##### 1000 kölemınde sandar tızbegın jalğastyru

[forward1000.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/sequence/forward1000.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recover missing or subsequent consecutive natural numbers using adjacency and a step of one. Crossing tens and hundreds does not change the rule; this differs from discovering an arbitrary pattern.

**User-friendly description (kk):** 1000 kölemındegı tızbektes sandardyñ kelesısın ne jetıspeitının tap, ondyq pen jüzdıkten ötkende de. Qadam ärqaşan bır.

##### 20 kölemınde tura sanau

[forward20.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/sequence/forward20.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Find successive natural numbers by adding one from any starting value within the range. Understand crossing a ten boundary instead of relying on reciting the sequence from one.

**User-friendly description (kk):** 20 kölemındegı kez kelgen sannan bastap, bır qosyp kelesı sandy tap, ondyqtan ötkende de.

##### Sanau kezındegı bır-bırıne säikestık

[oneToOne.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/sequence/oneToOne.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Counting a set establishes a one-to-one correspondence between each element and the next number word. Traversal order, spatial arrangement, and appearance do not affect cardinality if each element is counted exactly once.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Är zatqa bır ğana san atauyn säikestendır; eşqaisyn ötkızıp alma nemese ekı ret sanama. Sanau retı jalpy sandy özgertpeidı.

#### Qadamdap sanau

Skills: 4

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/steps/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Moving through the number sequence by fixed increments, connected with equal groups, tens, and hundreds rather than counting individual units.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Teñ toptardy är joly bırdei san qosyp sana. Är zatty jeke sanamai, 2, 5, 10 nemese 100 qadammen jyljy.

##### Ondyqtarmen sanau

[countBy10.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/steps/countBy10.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Each step of ten changes a number by one complete ten while preserving its remaining ones. Crossing a hundred requires recognizing that ten tens regroup into one hundred.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Är qadamda on qos; bırlıkter özgermeidı. Jüzdık şekarasynan ötkende on ondyq bır jüzdıkke ainalady.

##### Jüzdıktermen sanau

[countBy100.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/steps/countBy100.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A step of one hundred increases the number of complete hundreds by one; the tens and ones stay unchanged as long as the range permits. This relies on decimal place value.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Är qadamda jüz qos; ondyqtar men bırlıkter özgerıssız qalady.

##### Ekı-ekıden sanau

[countBy2.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/steps/countBy2.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Counting by twos repeatedly adds two, corresponding to equal pairs of objects. The number of pairs and the number of individual elements must be distinguished.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Är qadamda ekı qosyp, jūppen sana. Jūp sanyn zattardyñ jalpy sanynan ajyrat.

##### Bes-besten sanau

[countBy5.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/counting/steps/countBy5.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Counting by fives is repeated addition of equal groups containing five elements. The number of groups and total elements are related independently of visual representation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Är qadamda bes qosyp, besten toptalğan zattardyñ jalpy sanyn tap.

### Derekter

Groups: 3 · Skills: 14

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Formulating questions, collecting and classifying information, representing it in tables and charts, and drawing conclusions supported by the data.

#### Derekterdı jinau

Skills: 4

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/collection/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Formulating an investigation question, selecting classification attributes, counting occurrences, and recording observations.

##### Sanattardyñ jiılıgın sanau

[collectCounts.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/collection/collectCounts.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A category's frequency is the number of observations assigned to it. Counting must be consistent and unambiguous, and frequencies of exhaustive, nonoverlapping categories must sum to the total number of observations.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Baqylaularda är sanat neşe ret kezdesetının sanap, olardyñ qosyndysy jalpy baqylau sanyna teñ ekenın teksere alasyñ.

##### Baqylaulardy kestege jazu

[fillSimpleTable.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/collection/fillSimpleTable.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A table associates each recorded value with its labeled row, column, variable, category, and required unit. Its structure must preserve which observation each value describes and make later comparisons possible.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Baqylau nemese ölşeu nätijelerın joldary, bağandary, ataulary jäne ölşem bırlıkterı dūrys kestege jaza alasyñ.

##### Derekterdı zertteu sūrağyn tūjyrymdau

[formulateInvestigationQuestion.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/collection/formulateInvestigationQuestion.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A statistical question calls for observations or responses that may vary among members of a population. Distinguish a question requiring data collection from one whose answer follows uniquely from an already known arithmetic expression.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jauaptar ärtürlı boluy mümkın bolğandyqtan, bırneşe baqylau ne adamnan derek jinaudy qajet etetın sūraq qoia alasyñ.

##### Esepteu syzyqşalaryn jazu jäne oqu

[tallyMarks.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/collection/tallyMarks.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Tally marks or other agreed symbols represent counted observations in each category. Converting between symbolic marks and numerical frequencies must consistently follow the established encoding rule.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandy sanau syzyqşalary nemese kelısılgen tañbalar arqyly jazyp, olardy qaitadan dūrys sandarğa ainaldyra alasyñ.

#### Derekterdı tüsındıru

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/interpretation/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Drawing conclusions from quantitative data, computing comparisons, and identifying missing information.

##### Sanattar jiyntyğy men aiyrmalaryn salystyru

[compareCategories.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/interpretation/compareCategories.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Arithmetic on frequencies of different categories requires comparable units and a shared observation context. Their sum gives a combined count; their difference gives the numerical gap between categories.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Keste ne diagramma mänderımen tek salystyruğa bolatyn şamalardy paidalanyp, sanattardyñ jalpy sanyn nemese aiyrmasyn taba alasyñ.

##### Derekter negızınde qorytyndy jasau

[interpretConclusion.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/interpretation/interpretConclusion.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A conclusion must follow logically from the actual data values, categories, and scale. Distinguish direct observations, supported generalizations, and claims for which the data are insufficient.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Keste ne diagrammadağy naqty sandarğa süienıp, derekter körsetpegen närsenı qospai qorytyndy jasai alasyñ.

##### Jetıspeitın aqparatty anyqtau

[missingInformation.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/interpretation/missingInformation.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Data sufficiency is relative to a particular question: a necessary category, value, unit, time range, or sample information may be missing. Gaps must not be filled with arbitrary assumptions or invented numbers.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Derekter turaly sūraqqa jauap beru üşın qai sanat, män, ölşem bırlık, uaqyt aralyğy nemese basqa mälımet jetıspeitının anyqtai alasyñ.

#### Derekterdı ūsynu

Skills: 7

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/presentation/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Representing collected counts in tables, pictographs, and charts while correctly interpreting the scales and values of marks.

##### Bağandyq diagramma qūru

[buildBarChart.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/presentation/buildBarChart.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Values from a table are represented by bar heights on a consistent numerical scale, with clear category labels and units. All bars must use the same scale to avoid misleading comparisons.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Keste mänderınen sanat ataulary, dūrys ölşem bırlıkterı jäne barlyq bağanğa ortaq şkalasy bar bağandyq diagramma qūra alasyñ.

##### Piktogramma qūru

[buildPictograph.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/presentation/buildPictograph.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A pictograph must faithfully represent frequencies for labeled categories using an agreed key. Identical symbols must encode identical counts, and visual decoration must not distort relationships between values.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bırdei belgıler ärqaşan bırdei sandy bıldıretın aiqyn tüsındırmesı bar, sanattardyñ sanyn däl körsetetın surettı diagramma jasai alasyñ.

##### Ölşemderdı san tüzuıne belgıleu

[linePlotMeasurements.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/presentation/linePlotMeasurements.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A measurement line plot places observations on a common numerical axis; multiple marks at the same value represent repeated observations. The axis scale and correspondence between marks and frequencies must be explicit.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ölşeu nätijelerın san osıne qoiyp, bır män qaitalansa belgılerdı qabattap jäne şkalany bırdei saqtai alasyñ.

##### Bağandyq diagrammany oqu

[readBarChart.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/presentation/readBarChart.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The height or length of a bar encodes a numerical value according to a given scale and baseline. Comparisons require reading the axes and categories rather than relying on decorative bar width or area.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bağandyq diagramma mänderın bağan enınen emes, ataular men sandyq şkaladan oqyp, salystyra alasyñ.

##### Bır belgısı bır nysanğa säikes piktogrammany oqu

[readPictograph.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/presentation/readPictograph.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** In a pictograph where one symbol represents one object, frequencies are encoded by the count of symbols. Reading it requires the key, category labels, and number of symbols.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır belgı bır zatty bıldıretın surettı diagrammany tüsındırme men sanat ataularyna qarap, är sanatty dūrys sanai alasyñ.

##### Qarapaiym derekter kestesın oqu

[readSimpleTable.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/presentation/readSimpleTable.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpreting a table requires locating the relevant row, column, heading, and unit and relating them to the question. A bare number without its category or variable is not a complete interpretation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Kesteden dūrys joldy, bağandy, ataudy jäne ölşem bırlıgın tañdap, sūraqtyñ jauabyn taba alasyñ.

##### Masştabtalğan diagrammany oqu

[scaledChart.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/data/presentation/scaledChart.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** In scaled pictographs and charts, one mark may represent several items according to the key. To recover a count, multiply the number of marks by the units per mark rather than merely counting marks.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır belgı bırneşe zatty bıldıretın diagrammany tüsındırmege qarap, belgı sanyn är belgınıñ mänıne köbeitıp oqi alasyñ.

### Bölşekter

Groups: 4 · Skills: 19

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Fractions express part-to-whole relationships and positions on a number line. Their properties involve equal parts, numerator and denominator, equivalence, comparisons, and arithmetic operations; specific models and computational ranges depend on the learning context.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bölşekter bütınnıñ bölıkterın jäne san tüzuındegı oryndardy körsetedı. Olardy beineleudı, salystyrudy jäne esepteudı üiren.

#### Bölşekterge amaldar qoldanu

Skills: 2

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/arithmetic/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Changing the number of equal parts of the same whole through addition or subtraction with a common denominator.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır bütınnıñ teñ bölıkterın bıldıretın bölşekterdı bölımın özgertpei qos nemese azait.

##### Bır bütın şegınde bölımderı bırdei bölşekterdı qosu

[addLikeDenominators.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/arithmetic/addLikeDenominators.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** To add fractions with equal nonzero denominators, add the counts of like unit parts: a/b + c/b = (a+c)/b. The rule still holds when the sum exceeds one, although the Skill's examples stay within one whole.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bölımderı bırdei bölşekterdı qosqanda alymdaryn qos. Qosyndy bırden assa da bölıkterdıñ ölşemı özgermeidı.

##### Bır bütın şegınde bölımderı bırdei bölşekterdı azaitu

[subtractLikeDenominators.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/arithmetic/subtractLikeDenominators.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Subtracting like-denominator fractions removes unit parts without changing their size: a/b - c/b = (a-c)/b. The allowable range of numerators depends on the relevant number domain.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bölımderı bırdei bölşekterdı azaitqanda alymdaryn azait. Bölıkter sany kemidı, ölşemı özgermeidı.

#### Bölşekterdı salystyru

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/comparison/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Comparing the magnitudes of fractional parts relative to the same whole while holding either the numerator or denominator fixed.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır bütınnıñ bölşekterın teñ bölıkterdıñ şamasy nemese alynğan bölıkter sany boiynşa salystyr.

##### Alymdary bırdei bölşekterdı salystyru

[compareSameNumerator.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/comparison/compareSameNumerator.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Given the same positive numerator and unit whole, a larger denominator means smaller equal parts and therefore a smaller fraction. Comparing parts of different wholes by notation alone is invalid without a common unit.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Oñ alymdary bırdei bolsa, ülken bölım kışı bölıkterdı jäne sol bütınnıñ kışı bölşegın bıldıredı.

##### Bır bütınnıñ bırlık bölşekterın salystyru

[compareUnit.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/comparison/compareUnit.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The unit fraction 1/n denotes one of n equal parts of the same whole. Increasing the positive denominator reduces the size of that part; comparison presupposes the same unit.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Alym 1 bolsa, bır bütındı neğūrlym köp teñ bölıkke bölseñ, är bölık soğūrlym kışı: 1/4 < 1/2.

##### Bölımderı bırdei bölşekterdı modelder arqyly salystyru

[sameDenominatorModel.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/comparison/sameDenominatorModel.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** With the same positive denominator and whole, increasing the numerator increases the number of same-sized unit parts and hence the fraction's value. A visual model demonstrates but does not uniquely define the comparison method.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bölımderı bırdei bolsa, teñ bölıkterı köbırek bölşek ülken bolady. Suret 3/5 > 2/5 ekenın körsetedı.

#### Şamalardyñ bölıkterı

Skills: 2

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/portions/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Moving between a whole quantity and its unit fractional part through division and the inverse operation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Mölşerdıñ bölşek bölıgın tap nemese belgılı teñ bölık arqyly bütındı anyqta.

##### Şamanyñ 1/n bölıgın bölu arqyly tabu

[findUnitPart.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/portions/findUnitPart.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Finding 1/n of a quantity divides the whole into n equal parts for positive n. The resulting magnitude retains the physical unit and need not be an integer.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Mölşerdıñ 1/n bölıgın tabu üşın ony n teñ bölıkke böl. Bır bölık ölşem bırlıgınen de kışı boluy mümkın.

##### Belgılı bırlık bölıgı boiynşa bütındı tabu

[reconstructWhole.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/portions/reconstructWhole.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Given one of n equal parts of a whole, find the complete quantity by multiplying the part by positive n. This inverse relationship with division preserves the defined whole and its measurement unit.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Eger n teñ bölıktıñ bırın bılseñ, ony n-ge köbeitıp bütın mölşerdı tap.

#### Bölşekterdı körsetu

Skills: 12

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Fractional representation relative to a specified whole: unit and nonunit parts, conventional fraction notation, equivalent fractions, geometric models, and values greater than one.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tañdalğan bütınnıñ bölıkterın bölşekpen, suretpen nemese san tüzuınde körset, bırmen teñ ne ülken bölşekterdı de.

##### Bölşek bölımınıñ mağynasyn tüsındıru

[denominatorMeaning.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/denominatorMeaning.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The positive denominator specifies the number of equal parts in the chosen unit whole. It determines the magnitude of one part but not how many parts have been selected.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bölım bütınnıñ neşe teñ bölıkke bölıngenın körsetedı. Ol bölıktıñ ölşemın anyqtaidy, alynğan bölıkter sanyn emes.

##### Teñ bölşekterdı körnekı modeldermen körsetu

[equivalentVisual.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/equivalentVisual.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Equivalent fractions denote the same part of the same whole despite different numerators and denominators. Multiplying both by the same nonzero factor preserves value, as can be shown using area or line models.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ärtürlı bölşekter bır bütınnıñ teñ mölşerın bıldıruı mümkın, mysaly 1/2 jäne 2/4.

##### Bırden ülken bölşekterdı körsetu

[fractionGreaterThanOne.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/fractionGreaterThanOne.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** An improper fraction whose numerator exceeds its positive denominator is greater than one. It can be represented as a mixed number or a point to the right of one on a positive number line; the unit whole stays fixed.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Alym bölımnen ülken bolsa, bölşek bırden ülken. Ony bütın bölıktermen, aralas sanmen nemese san tüzuınde körset.

##### Bırneşe teñ bölıkterı bar bölşekterdı modeldeu

[nonUnitModel.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/nonUnitModel.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The fraction a/b combines a selected count a of unit parts with their size 1/b for nonzero b. All parts refer to the same whole, and the numerator may equal or exceed the denominator.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır bütınnıñ bırneşe teñ bölıgın bırıktırıp, 3/4 siiaqty bölşektı körset. Bölıkter bır bütınge teñ ne odan köp boluy mümkın.

##### 0 men 1 arasyndağy bölşekterdı san säulesıne ornalastyru

[numberLine.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/numberLine.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** For positive b, subdividing the unit interval into b equal parts locates a/b by moving a such steps from zero. The resulting number-line representation must preserve scale and numerical order.

**User-friendly description (kk):** San tüzuındegı 0 men 1 arasyn teñ qadamdarğa bölıp, 3/5 siiaqty bölşektıñ ornyn tap.

##### Bölşek alymynyñ mağynasyn tüsındıru

[numeratorMeaning.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/numeratorMeaning.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The numerator specifies the count of unit parts determined by the denominator. With a fixed positive denominator, increasing a nonnegative numerator increases the fraction, possibly above one.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Alym neşe teñ bölık alynğanyn körsetedı. Bölım bırdei bolsa, köbırek bölık ülken bölşektı bıldıredı.

##### Bır bütındı n/n türınde körsetu

[oneAsFraction.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/oneAsFraction.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** For nonzero n, n/n equals one whole: n parts of size 1/n reconstruct the unit. This is true independently of the partition or visual model.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Barlyq teñ bölıkter bırıgıp bır bütın qūraidy: 2/2, 3/3 jäne 5/5 bärı 1-ge teñ.

##### Ondyq ülesterdı 10-ğa bölumen bailanystyru

[tenthsAsDivision.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/tenthsAsDivision.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A tenth results from partitioning the same whole into ten equal parts, with value 1/10 of that whole. Dividing by ten and representing the result as common or decimal fractions preserve the chosen unit.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Onnan bır — bütınnıñ on teñ bölıgınıñ bırı. Bütındı 10-ğa bölseñ 1/10 şyğady, ony 0,1 dep te jazady.

##### 1/n bırlık bölşekterın modeldeu

[unitFractionModel.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/unitFractionModel.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** For positive integer n, 1/n represents one of n equal parts of a specified whole. In area, length, and discrete-set models, equality concerns the relevant magnitude, not necessarily identical shapes.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Pışın, ūzyndyq nemese zat toptarymen 1/n bır bütınnıñ n teñ bölıgınıñ bırı ekenın körset.

##### Bırlık bölşekterdı oqu jäne jazu

[unitFractionRead.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/unitFractionRead.ts)
