**Methodological description (English):** A unit fraction has numerator one and a positive denominator stating how many equal parts form the whole. Half, third, and quarter correspond to the fractions 1/2, 1/3, and 1/4.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Alymy 1 bolatyn bölşekterdı oqyp, jaz: 1/2 (jarty), 1/3 (üşten bır), 1/4 (törtten bır).

##### Bütındı, teñ jäne teñ emes bölıkterdı ajyratu

[wholeAndEqualParts.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/wholeAndEqualParts.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A fractional part is defined by dividing the same whole into parts of equal magnitude. Arbitrary pieces need not be halves; the visual form of the whole does not remove the equal-parts requirement.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır bütındı tañdap, ony teñ ölşemdı bölıkterge böl. Ölşemderı ärtürlı bölıkter sol bütınnıñ teñ ülesterı emes.

##### Bölık ölşemınıñ bütınge täueldılıgın tüsındıru

[wholeDependence.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/fractions/representation/wholeDependence.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The same fractional notation denotes the same proportion of different wholes, but its absolute magnitude depends on the size of each whole. Comparing parts from different wholes requires a shared unit or comparable magnitude.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bölşek bütınnıñ ülesın körsetedı. Ülken bütınnıñ jartysy kışı bütınnıñ jartysynan ülken.

### Geometriia

Groups: 10 · Skills: 35

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Spatial relationships, properties of plane figures and solids, lines and angles, geometric transformations, and measurement of perimeter and area.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Oryndardy, syzyqtardy, jazyq figuralar men denelerdı, būryştardy, qozğalysty, perimetr men audandy zertte.

#### Būryştar

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/angles/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Angles as relationships between rays and as measures of turn, with the right angle serving as a reference for classification.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Būryştardy būrylys dep qarap, tık būryşpen salystyr jäne türlerın tany.

##### Būryştardy būrylu retınde salystyru

[angleAsTurn.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/angles/angleAsTurn.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Angle magnitude describes the turn between rays sharing an endpoint and does not depend on how long the rays are drawn. A right angle is one quarter of a full turn; acute and obtuse angles are compared with it.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı säulenıñ arasyndağy būrylu şamasyn salystyr. Qabyrğalardy ūzyn syzu būryşty ülkeitpeidı.

##### Süiır, tık jäne doğal būryştardy ajyratu

[angleTypes.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/angles/angleTypes.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** An acute angle has measure strictly between 0 and 90 degrees, a right angle measures 90 degrees, and an obtuse angle lies strictly between 90 and 180 degrees. The drawn lengths of the arms do not affect classification.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Süiır (90°-tan kem), tık (90°) jäne doğal (90° pen 180° arasynda) būryştardy ajyrat.

##### Tık būryştardy anyqtau jäne tekseru

[rightAngle.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/angles/rightAngle.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A right angle measures 90 degrees regardless of ray orientation. A reference or measuring tool can verify this property; rotating the drawing does not change the angle type.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Kölbeu salynsa da tık būryştardy tauyp tekser. Är tık būryş 90 gradus.

#### Audan

Skills: 4

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/area/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The extent of a planar region occupied by a figure, modeled using unit squares, rectangles, and decomposition of composite shapes.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jazyq figuralardyñ ışkı audanyn şarşy bırlıkpen ölşe, sonyñ ışınde tıktörtbūryş pen qūramdas figuralardy.

##### Audandy bırlık şarşylarmen jabu retınde tüsınu

[areaAsCovering.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/area/areaAsCovering.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Area measures the size of a plane region in square units; covering it with identical squares without gaps or overlap yields a numerical measure. Equal area after changing shape does not imply equal perimeter.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Audan figuranyñ qanşa jazyq oryndy alatynyn körsetedı. Ony bırdei bırlık şarşylarmen bos orynsyz jäne qabattastyrmai jap.

##### Qūrama tıkbūryşty figuranyñ audanyn tabu

[compositeArea.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/area/compositeArea.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Area is additive for nonoverlapping regions: a compound figure may be partitioned into rectangles whose areas sum to the original. The partition must cover the figure without gaps or double-counted overlaps.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tıktörtbūryştardan qūralğan figurany qabattaspaityn bölıkterge bölıp, audandaryn qaitalamai qos.

##### Bırlık şarşylardy sanau arqyly audandy anyqtau

[countUnitSquares.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/area/countUnitSquares.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** When a plane region consists of nonoverlapping unit squares, its area is their count. Distinguish the number of complete squares from side lengths, and account for fractional square units when needed.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Figura ışındegı bırlık şarşylardy sanap audan tap, qajet bolsa şarşy bölıkterın de esepte.

##### Tıktörtbūryş audanyn qabyrğalarynyñ köbeitındısımen bailanystyru

[rectangleAreaModel.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/area/rectangleAreaModel.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The area of a rectangle is the product of adjacent side lengths expressed in a common length unit. A grid of congruent unit squares explains the formula through row and column counts.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tıktörtbūryştyñ audany — ūzyndyğy men enınıñ köbeitındısı. Bırdei şarşylardan qūralğan qatarlar men bağandar būl formulanyñ nege dūrys ekenın körsetedı.

#### Şeñberler men döñgelekter

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/circles/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The circumference as the boundary of a disk, its center, radius and diameter, and constructing a circle at a fixed distance from its center.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Şeñber men boialğan döñgelektı, ortalyğyn, radiusyn, diametrın jäne şeñber syzudy üiren.

##### Şeñber men döñgelektı ajyratu

[circleDisk.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/circles/circleDisk.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A circle is the set of points in a plane at a fixed distance from a center; a disk includes those points and its enclosed region. Distinguish boundary from filled area, and circumference from the disk's area.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Şeñberdıñ qisyq şekarasyn ışındegı döñgelek aimaqtan ajyrat. Şekara audan emes.

##### Berılgen radiusy bar şeñberdı tsirkulmen syzu

[drawCircle.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/circles/drawCircle.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** When constructing a circle, a compass point establishes its center and a fixed opening establishes its radius. Changing the opening changes the radius; the principle is independent of a particular compass design.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tsirkulmen tañdalğan ortalyq pen radiusy bar şeñber syz. Tsirkul aşyluy radiusty belgıleidı.

##### Tsentr, radius jäne diametrdıñ bailanysy

[radiusDiameter.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/circles/radiusDiameter.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A circle's center determines its constant distance to every point on the circle; a radius connects center to circle, and a diameter passes through the center to join two circle points. Diameter length is twice radius.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Şeñberdıñ ortalyğyn, radiusyn, diametrın tap. Diametr ortalyqtan ötedı jäne radiustan ekı ese ūzyn.

#### Jazyq figuralar

Skills: 5

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/figures/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Properties of polygons and other plane figures that remain independent of scale or orientation, and composing shapes from parts.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jazyq figuralardy qabyrğasy, töbesı jäne qasietı boiynşa tanyp, bölıkterden jaña figura qūrastyr.

##### Jazyq figuralardy qūrastyru jäne bölşekteu

[composeDecomposeShapes.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/figures/composeDecomposeShapes.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Decomposition partitions a figure into nonoverlapping pieces without gaps, and recombining them reconstructs the original figure. Rearrangement preserves the combined area but may change the outer boundary and perimeter.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jazyq figurany bos orynsyz, qabattastyrmai bölıp, qaita qūrastyr. Audany saqtalady, syrtqy şekarasy özgeruı mümkın.

##### Negızgı jazyq figuralardy tanu

[identify2dShapes.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/figures/identify2dShapes.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A figure's geometric class depends on its properties, not its size, color, or orientation in a drawing. A rotated square remains a square and is a special case of a rectangle.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Figura būrylsa, ölşemı ne tüsı özgerse de tany. Şarşy da tıktörtbūryştyñ bır türı.

##### Köpbūryştar men olardyñ bölıkterın tanu

[polygon.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/figures/polygon.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A polygon is a plane figure bounded by a closed polygonal chain of straight segments meeting at vertices. Not every closed curve forms a polygon; the boundary differs from its interior region.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Köpbūryşty töbelerde tüiısetın tüzu qabyrğalarmen qorşalğan tūiyq figura retınde tany.

##### Figuralardy qabyrğalary men töbelerı boiynşa jıkteu

[shapeAttributes.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/figures/shapeAttributes.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Classify polygons by their side and vertex counts and defining geometric properties. A simple polygon has equally many sides and vertices, though orientation, side lengths, and shape can vary.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Köpbūryştardy qabyrğalary men töbelerınıñ sany jäne qasietı boiynşa jıkte, surettıñ bağytymen emes.

##### Üşbūryştardyñ, tıktörtbūryştardyñ jäne şarşylardyñ qasietterı

[triangleRectangleSquare.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/figures/triangleRectangleSquare.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Triangles, rectangles, and squares are characterized by relations among sides and angles. A square is a rectangle with all sides equal; geometric categories can be nested rather than mutually exclusive.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Üşbūryş, tıktörtbūryş, şarşyny qabyrğalary men būryştarynan tany. Är şarşy — tıktörtbūryş.

#### Tüzuler men syzyqtar

Skills: 5

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/lines/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Points, lines, rays, segments, other line types, their components, relative positions, and graphical representations.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Nüktelerdı, tüzulerdı, qisyqtardy, säulelerdı, kesındılerdı jäne olardyñ qatynasyn tany.

##### Tūiyq jäne tūiyq emes syzyqtardy tanu

[closedOpenLines.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/lines/closedOpenLines.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A closed line has no distinct start and end points, whereas an open line does not close into a loop. Not every closed line is polygonal, and a line is not the region it encloses.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Syzyq tūiyq kontur qūra ma, älde aşyq pa, anyqta. Tūiyq syzyq ärqaşan tüzu qabyrğalardan tūrmaidy.

##### Nükteler men syzyq türlerın ajyratu

[linesAndPoints.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/lines/linesAndPoints.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A point specifies a position without dimension, a straight line extends infinitely both ways, a general curve need not consist of straight segments, and a polygonal chain consists of consecutive segments. Drawn marks are models, not the abstract objects themselves.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Nüktenı, tüzudı, qisyq syzyqty jäne tüzu kesındılerden tūratyn synyq syzyqty ajyrat. Suret tek olardy beineleidı.

##### Parallel jäne perpendikuliar tüzulerdı tanu

[parallelPerpendicular.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/lines/parallelPerpendicular.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinct parallel lines in the same plane do not intersect; perpendicular lines meet at a right angle. These relations depend on geometric structure, not merely a familiar horizontal or vertical drawing.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Eşqaşan qiylyspaityn parallel tüzulerdı jäne tık būryşpen qiylysatyn perpendikuliar tüzulerdı, kölbeu bolsa da tany.

##### Säulelerdı, kesındılerdı jäne tüzulerdı ajyratu

[ray.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/lines/ray.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A line extends indefinitely in both directions; a ray has one endpoint and extends indefinitely in one direction; a segment has two endpoints. Drawing orientation does not change these properties.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı bağytta şeksız sozylatyn tüzu, bır nükteden şyğatyn säule jäne ekı ūşy bar kesındını ajyrat.

##### Kesındılerdı salu jäne belgıleu

[segment.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/lines/segment.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A line segment is the part of a straight line between two endpoints, including those points, and can be named by them. Construction preserves straightness; its length is the distance between endpoints.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı ūştyñ arasynda tüzu kesındı syz, ūştaryn belgıle, ūzyndyğyn tüsın.

#### Keñıstıkte bağdarlau

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/orientation/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Verbal descriptions of relative positions and movements, following and giving route instructions, and navigating a simple grid.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bağyttar, marşruttar jäne qarapaiym kartalar arqyly zattardyñ ornyn, oryndar arasyndağy joldy sipatta.

##### Qarapaiym torly kartalardy oqu jäne syzu

[gridMapNavigation.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/orientation/gridMapNavigation.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A grid defines a discrete spatial system with consistent directions or coordinates. Plans, paths, and end positions must follow the same reference conventions; cell size and orientation affect interpretation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tor közdı kartany oqy ne sal, oryndar men joldardy belgıle. Bağyt pen masştabty bırdei saqta.

##### Salystyrmaly ornalasudy sipattau

[positionWords.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/orientation/positionWords.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Spatial relations are defined relative to an object, observer, or coordinate frame. Left, right, and ahead depend on the reference point; distinguish relative orientation from absolute coordinates.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sol, oñ, joğary, artynda, aldynda degen sözdermen oryndy ait. Qarau bağyty özgerse, jauap ta özgeruı mümkın.

##### Bağytty tüsındıru jäne nūsqaumen jüru

[spatialOrientationPath.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/orientation/spatialOrientationPath.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A route is an ordered sequence of moves and turns relative to a fixed initial orientation. Changing command order or starting direction may change the destination even if the set of steps stays the same.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jol nūsqaularyn dūrys retımen ber ne orynda. Bastapqy bağyt nemese būrylystar retı özgerse, barar jer de özgeredı.

#### Perimetr

Skills: 4

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/perimeter/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The length of a polygon's closed boundary as the sum of its sides, including rectangles and squares.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Köpbūryşty ainala ötetın qaşyqtyqty barlyq qabyrğa ūzyndyqtaryn qosyp ölşe.

##### Köpbūryş perimetrın qabyrğalaryn qosu arqyly ölşeu

[measurePerimeter.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/perimeter/measurePerimeter.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The perimeter of a polygon is the sum of the lengths of all successive sides of its closed boundary. It is a linear measurement expressed in length units, unlike the area of its interior.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Köpbūryştyñ barlyq qabyrğalaryn qosyp, ūzyndyq bırlıgımen perimetrın tap.

##### Tıktörtbūryştyñ perimetrın esepteu

[rectanglePerimeter.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/perimeter/rectanglePerimeter.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so a rectangle with side lengths a and b has perimeter P = 2(a+b). This abbreviates the sum of four side lengths, not the area.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tıktörtbūryştyñ tört qabyrğasyn qosyp ne ūzyndyğy men enınıñ qosyndysyn ekı eselep perimetr tap.

##### Şarşynyñ perimetrın esepteu

[squarePerimeter.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/perimeter/squarePerimeter.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** All four sides of a square are equal, so its perimeter is four times the side length, P = 4a. Perimeter is a linear magnitude distinct from area a².

**User-friendly description (kk):** Şarşynyñ bır qabyrğasynyñ ūzyndyğyn törtke köbeitıp perimetrın tap.

##### Tıktörtbūryştyñ belgısız qabyrğasyn perimetr arqyly tabu

[unknownSideFromPerimeter.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/perimeter/unknownSideFromPerimeter.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** For a rectangle, P = 2(a+b) permits recovering an unknown side from the perimeter and known other side: b = P/2 - a. The result must be positive and expressed in compatible length units.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tıktörtbūryştyñ perimetrı men bır qabyrğasy belgılı bolsa, ekınşısın esepte.

#### Perimetr men audannyñ bailanysy

Skills: 2

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/perimeterArea/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Perimeter measures the boundary and area measures the interior; the same value for one does not uniquely determine the other.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Figurany ainala ūzyndyq pen ışındegı audannyñ aiyrmasyn tüsın.

##### Perimetrı men audany ärtürlı figuralar qūrastyru

[areaPerimeterContrast.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/perimeterArea/areaPerimeterContrast.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Equal perimeter lengths do not determine area: rectangles 1 × 6 and 2 × 5 both have perimeter 14 but areas 6 and 10. Rectangles 1 × 6 and 2 × 3 both have area 6 but different perimeters.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Perimetrı bırdei, audany ärtürlı nemese audany bırdei, perimetrı ärtürlı figuralar qūrastyr.

##### Ölşeu üşın perimetrdı nemese audandy tañdau

[perimeterVsArea.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/perimeterArea/perimeterVsArea.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Perimeter measures the length of a closed plane boundary in length units, while area measures the enclosed region in square units. Neither determines the other automatically, and they require different measurement procedures.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Şekarany ūzyndyq bırlıgımen ölşeuge perimetrdı, ışkı bölıktı şarşy bırlıkpen ölşeuge audandy tañda.

#### Keñıstıktık figuralar

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/solids/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguishing three-dimensional solids from flat depictions and identifying their surfaces, faces, edges, and vertices.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Keñıstıktegı denelerdı, olardyñ jaqtaryn, qyrlaryn, töbelerın jäne qisyq betterın tany.

##### Negızgı keñıstıktık figuralardy tanu

[identify3dSolids.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/solids/identify3dSolids.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify solids by their surface structure and the number or shape of faces, bases, edges, and vertices where applicable. Perspective drawings can distort proportions; geometric properties determine the solid's class.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Denelerdı betterı, jaqtary, qyrlary men töbelerı arqyly basqa qyrynan salynsa da tany.

##### Kölemdı denelerdıñ betterındegı jazyq figuralardy tanu

[shapeOnSolidSurface.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/solids/shapeOnSolidSurface.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Plane figures can coincide with the faces of solids or their plane sections, but the solid itself remains three-dimensional. Distinguish a two-dimensional part of a surface from the entire three-dimensional object.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Denenıñ jaqtary men qimalarynan jazyq figuralar tap. Jazyq jaq bükıl keñıstıktık dene emes.

##### Tekşeler men tıkbūryşty parallelepipedterdıñ jaqtary, qyrlary jäne töbelerı

[spatialSolidsAttributes.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/solids/spatialSolidsAttributes.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A cube and a rectangular cuboid each have six faces, twelve edges, and eight vertices. A cube is a special case with equal edge lengths; a drawing may show only some of the solid's elements.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tekşe men tıkbūryşty parallelepipedte 6 jaq, 12 qyr, 8 töbe bar. Tekşenıñ barlyq qyry teñ.

#### Geometriialyq türlendıruler

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/transformations/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Changes in a shape's position through rotation, translation, and reflection, along with symmetry about an axis.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Figuralardy jyljyt, būr jäne şağyldyr, qai qasietterı saqtalatynyn baiqa.

##### Simmetriia osterın tabu jäne şağyldyrudy tolyqtyru

[reflectionSymmetry.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/transformations/reflectionSymmetry.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** An axis of symmetry defines a reflection that maps a figure onto itself. Corresponding points lie on opposite sides at equal perpendicular distances; points on the axis remain fixed.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Figurany ainadağydai ekı bölıkke böletın simmetriia osın tap nemese şağyluyn aiaqta.

##### Figuralardy jyljytu jäne şağyldyru

[translationsReflections.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/transformations/translationsReflections.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A translation moves every point of a figure by the same vector, preserving lengths and orientation. Reflection in a line also preserves lengths but reverses orientation; neither changes area or perimeter.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Figurany būrmai jyljyt nemese tüzuge qatysty şağyldyr. Ūzyndyq, audan, perimetr özgermeidı.

##### Şirek, jarty jäne üş şirek ainalymdar

[turnsQuarters.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/geometry/transformations/turnsQuarters.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Quarter, half, and three-quarter turns equal 90, 180, and 270 degrees. Rotation direction affects final orientation, though some final positions admit more than one equivalent description of the turn.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sağat tılımen ne oğan qarsy şirek, jarty nemese üş şirek ainalym jasap bağytty özgert.

### Ölşeu

Groups: 5 · Skills: 22

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Measurement of physical quantities by comparison with units, instruments, and scales, covering length, mass, capacity, temperature, and consistent use of units.

#### Syiymdylyq

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/capacity/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The volume of liquid that a container can hold, its measurement in liters and milliliters, and comparisons of capacities.

##### Ydystar syiymdylyğyn qūiu nemese ölşeu arqyly salystyru

[capacityConcept.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/capacity/capacityConcept.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Capacity is the maximum volume a container can hold. It can be compared by transferring contents under consistent conditions or measuring volume; height or shape alone does not determine capacity.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ydystardyñ syiymdylyğyn biıktıgıne ne pışınıne ğana qarap emes, sūiyqtyqty qūiyp nemese ölşep salystyra alasyñ.

##### Syiymdylyqty litrmen ölşeu jäne bağalau

[liter.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/capacity/liter.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A liter is a volume unit commonly used for container capacity. Estimation must use an appropriate unit reference; container shape alone does not reliably determine capacity without other dimensions.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır litrdı ülgı etıp, ydystyñ syiymdylyğyn litrmen şamalap ne ölşep anyqtai alasyñ.

##### Millilitr men litrdıñ bailanysy

[milliliter.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/capacity/milliliter.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** One liter equals 1,000 milliliters. Different numerical unit representations can express the same volume or capacity; conversion must preserve the factor of one thousand.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Syiymdylyqty millilitrmen ölşep, 1 litr = 1000 millilitr ekenın bılıp, litr men millilitrdı özara ainaldyra alasyñ.

#### Jalpy ölşeu dağdylary

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/general/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** General principles for choosing units, reconciling measurements, and calculating with comparable quantities.

##### Ūzyndyq, massa nemese syiymdylyqqa sai ölşem bırlıkterın tañdau

[chooseAppropriateUnit.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/general/chooseAppropriateUnit.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Choose a measurement unit based on the physical quantity, size of the object, and needed precision. The choice must be justified without mixing dimensions or copying a conventional example uncritically.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Nenı jäne qanşalyqty däl ölşeitınıñe qarai ūzyndyq, massa ne syiymdylyq üşın qolaily ölşem bırlıgın tañdai alasyñ.

##### Ortaq ölşem bırlıkterınıñ qajettılıgın tüsındıru

[standardUnitPurpose.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/general/standardUnitPurpose.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Measurements can be compared meaningfully only with their quantities and units. Equivalent units require conversion to a common scale; equal numerals in different units can represent different magnitudes.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ölşemderdı salystyru üşın nege bırlıkterdı säikestendıru keregın tüsındırıp, tek sandardy emes, qajet bolsa bırlıkterdı ainaldyra alasyñ.

##### Säikes ölşem bırlıkterımen mätındık esepterdı şeşu

[wordProblemsMeasures.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/general/wordProblemsMeasures.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Calculations with measured quantities require compatible units and dimensionally valid operations. Addition or subtraction is meaningful only for commensurable quantities, and the result must retain the appropriate unit and interpretation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ölşengen şamalarğa qatysty tūrmystyq esepterdı säikes bırlıktermen şyğaryp, jauapta dūrys bırlıktı körsete alasyñ.

#### Ūzyndyq

Skills: 11

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/length/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Direct and instrument-based comparison of lengths, metric units of differing magnitudes, and operations on homogeneous length quantities.

##### Säikes bırlıkterdegı ūzyndyqtardy qosu jäne azaitu

[addSubtractLengths.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/length/addSubtractLengths.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Adding and subtracting lengths requires quantities of the same physical dimension. Convert to a common scale or explicitly account for unit changes; the result must remain a length.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ūzyndyqtardy säikes ölşem bırlıkterıne ainaldyrğan soñ qosyp ne azaityp, jauapty dūrys ūzyndyq bırlıgımen jaza alasyñ.

##### Ūzyndyqtardy tıkelei jäne janama salystyru

[compareLength.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/length/compareLength.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Lengths can be compared by aligning their initial endpoints or through a common intermediate measure. Comparison concerns endpoint separation, not an object's placement or visible thickness.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Zattar men kesındılerdıñ ūzyndyqtaryn ūştaryn turalap nemese ortaq ölşemmen salystyra alasyñ, ornyna ne qalyñdyğyna qarap emes.

##### Detsimetr men santimetrdı türlendıru

[decimeters.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/length/decimeters.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** One decimeter equals ten centimeters. Converting between them multiplies or divides the numerical measure by ten while preserving the actual length; always state the unit.

**User-friendly description (kk):** 1 detsimetr = 10 santimetr ekenın jäne ūzyndyq özgermeitının bılıp, detsimetr men santimetrdı özara ainaldyra alasyñ.

##### Berılgen ūzyndyqtağy kesındılerdı santimetrmen syzu

[drawSegmentCentimeters.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/length/drawSegmentCentimeters.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Construct a straight line segment of a specified length in centimeters: align a ruler at zero, mark the required endpoint, and draw the segment with the correct length. This is a construction competency distinct from reading the length of an existing segment.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Syzğyştyñ nölınen bastap, berılgen santimetrlık ūzyndyqqa sai ekınşı ūşyn belgılep, tüzu kesındı syza alasyñ.

##### Ūzyndyqty bağalau jäne ölşeumen tekseru

[estimateLength.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/length/estimateLength.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Estimate a length against a reference or a known measure, then verify with an instrument. Interpret discrepancies between estimated and measured values using consistent units.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tanys ölşemdı ülgı etıp zattyñ ūzyndyğyn şamalap, keiın qūralmen ölşep, ekı nätijenı bırdei bırlıkpen salystyra alasyñ.

##### Ülken qaşyqtyqty kilometrmen ölşeu jäne metrge ainaldyru

[kilometers.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/length/kilometers.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** One kilometer equals one thousand meters. It is convenient for large distances, but an appropriate unit depends on context and precision. Conversion does not change the distance.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Alys qaşyqtyqtarğa kilometrdı qoldanyp, 1 km = 1000 m ekenın bılıp, kilometr men metrdı özara ainaldyra alasyñ.

##### Kesındılerdı santimetrmen ölşeu

[measureCentimeters.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/length/measureCentimeters.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine the length of an existing straight segment in centimeters by aligning a ruler's zero mark with one endpoint and reading the other endpoint. Count intervals rather than printed labels; drawing a new segment is a separate competency.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Daiyn tüzu kesındınıñ ūzyndyğyn santimetrmen ölşei alasyñ: bır ūşyn syzğyştyñ nölıne keltırıp, ekınşı ūşyndağy bölıktı oqisyñ.

##### Metr, detsimetr jäne santimetrdıñ bailanysy

[meters.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/length/meters.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** 1 m = 10 dm = 100 cm: these length units are related by powers of ten. Different unit expressions for the same length must be equivalent; mixed-unit measurement requires consistent scaling.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ūzyndyqty metr, detsimetr nemese santimetrmen ölşep, 1 m = 10 dm = 100 sm qatynasymen ainaldyra alasyñ.

##### Millimetrmen ölşeu jäne santimetrmen bailanystyru

[millimeters.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/length/millimeters.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** One millimeter is one tenth of a centimeter; the same length can be expressed equivalently in millimeters and centimeters. Unit choice should reflect the required precision without changing the measured length.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qysqa ūzyndyqtardy millimetrmen ölşep, 10 mm = 1 sm ekenın bılıp, millimetr men santimetrdı özara ainaldyra alasyñ.

##### Ūzyndyqty qaitalanatyn standartty emes bırlıktermen ölşeu

[nonstandardLength.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/length/nonstandardLength.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Measuring length means counting consecutive equal unit intervals along an object without gaps or overlaps. The numerical result depends on the unit, but the physical length does not.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ūzyndyğy bırdei ölşeu bırlıkterın sañylausyz jäne qabattastyrmai tızıp, ūzyndyqty ölşei alasyñ; bırlıktıñ ūzyndyğy özgerse, olardyñ sany da özgeretının tüsınesıñ.

##### Syzğyşty qoldanu

[useRuler.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/length/useRuler.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use a ruler as a measurement instrument: recognize its zero mark and equal scale intervals, align the scale with a straight segment, and read the numbered centimeter marks. Basic use starts at zero; determining the length of an unknown segment is assessed separately.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Syzğyştağy nöl belgısın tauyp, ony tüzu kesındınıñ boiyna turalap qoiyp, aralyğy bırdei santimetrlık bölıkterdı oqi alasyñ.

#### Massa

Skills: 4

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/mass/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Mass as a physical quantity, its comparison with balances, reading its numerical value from instruments, and relationships among established units of mass. Mass is not identical to weight as a force.

##### Esepterde tsentner men kilogramdy qoldanu

[centnerKilogram.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/mass/centnerKilogram.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Where the metric centner is used, one centner equals 100 kilograms, while one metric tonne equals 1,000 kilograms. The centner is context-dependent, not universal across countries or curricula.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Metrlık tsentner qoldanylatyn esepterde 1 tsentner = 100 kilogramm ekenın, 1000 emes ekenın bılıp eseptei alasyñ.

##### Massalardy tarazymen salystyru

[compareMass.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/mass/compareMass.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** On an equal-arm balance, a greater mass outweighs a smaller one under comparable conditions, and balance indicates equal masses. Physical volume or apparent size alone does not determine mass.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ülken körıngen zat mındettı türde auyr dep oilamai, zattardyñ massasyn tarazymen salystyra alasyñ.

##### Kilogramm men gramnyñ bailanysy

[kilogramGram.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/mass/kilogramGram.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** One kilogram equals 1,000 grams. Changing between these mass units alters the numerical measure but not the physical mass.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Massany kilogramm ne grammen ölşep, 1 kilogramm = 1000 gramm ekenın bılıp bırlıkterdı auystyra alasyñ.

##### Tarazy körsetkışın oqu jäne massany bırlıkpen jazu

[weighObject.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/mass/weighObject.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A mass reading is meaningful only with its unit and the instrument's scale. Interpret divisions, graduation intervals, and the physical quantity being measured.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tarazy şkalasyn oqyp, zattyñ massasyn anyqtap, nätijenı dūrys ölşem bırlıgımen jaza alasyñ.

#### Temperatura

Skills: 1

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/temperature/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Temperature as a physical quantity, its reading from a thermometer scale, interpretation of scale divisions, and correct temperature-unit notation; whether a reading is positive or negative does not determine membership in this group.

##### Termometrden terıs emes temperaturalardy oqu

[readTemperature.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/measurement/temperature/readTemperature.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A temperature scale relates numerical marks to temperature values in specified units, such as degrees Celsius. Reading intermediate divisions relies on the scale and must include the measurement unit.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Termometr şkalasynan nöl gradus jäne odan joğary temperaturany oqyp, °C siiaqty dūrys ölşem bırlıgın jaza alasyñ.

### Aqşa

Groups: 2 · Skills: 6

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/money/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Applications of arithmetic to monetary denominations, composing and comparing amounts, calculating costs and change, and selecting purchases within a budget.

#### Aqşa somalary

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/money/denominations/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Monetary value represented by coins and banknotes of a specific currency, equivalent denomination combinations, and comparisons between amounts.

##### Aqşa somalaryn salystyru

[compareAmounts.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/money/denominations/compareAmounts.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare the total face value, not the number or physical size of coins and banknotes. Values within one currency can be combined in consistent units, including fractional currency units where applicable.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır valiutadağy ekı aqşalai somany monetalardyñ sanyna ne kölemıne emes, olardyñ qūnyn qosyp salystyra alasyñ.

##### Aqşa somasyn qūrastyru

[composeAmount.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/money/denominations/composeAmount.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The same monetary amount can be composed from different combinations of available denominations in one currency. Exchanging coins or notes must preserve total value, and denominations that do not exist cannot be used.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır valiutada şynymen qoldanylatyn monetalar men banknottardy ärtürlı bırıktırıp, bırdei aqşa somasyn qūra alasyñ.

##### Monetalar men banknottardyñ nominaldaryn tanu

[recognizeDenominations.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/money/denominations/recognizeDenominations.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A denomination is the established monetary value of a coin or banknote in a specified currency; physical size, material, color, and printed symbols do not independently determine it. Valid denominations depend on the monetary system.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Belgılı bır valiutadağy ärtürlı moneta men banknottyñ nominalyn kölemı men tüsıne qaramai tani alasyñ.

#### Satyp alular

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/money/transactions/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Using monetary calculations for unit prices, quantities, purchase totals, change, and limited budgets.

##### Biudjetke sai satyp alulardy tañdau

[budgetConstraint.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/money/transactions/budgetConstraint.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Whether a set of purchases is affordable depends on the sum of its costs relative to the available budget. Each item being individually affordable does not make the entire set affordable; quantities and the total-spending limit must be considered.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Barlyq satyp aludyñ qūnyn qosyp, biudjetten aspai qandai tauardy qanşa aluğa bolatynyn anyqtai alasyñ.

##### Qaitarym aqşany esepteu

[calculateChange.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/money/transactions/calculateChange.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Change is the difference between the amount actually paid and the amount due, provided the payment is sufficient. It must be expressed in the same currency, and adding the change to the purchase price checks the result.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Satyp aluğa jetkılıktı aqşa bergen soñ qaitarylatyn aqşany eseptep, ony tauar qūnymen teksere alasyñ.

##### Bırlık bağasy men sany boiynşa jalpy qūndy esepteu

[unitPriceTotal.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/money/transactions/unitPriceTotal.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** When the unit price is fixed, total cost equals unit price multiplied by quantity; knowing any two of these values can determine the third. Monetary totals must be distinguished from prices per unit and the quantity units kept consistent.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır zattyñ bağasy men sany boiynşa jalpy qūndy eseptei alasyñ nemese qalğan ekı mänı belgılı bolsa, belgısız bağany ne sandy taba alasyñ.

### Natural sandar

Groups: 5 · Skills: 27

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** How natural numbers express quantity, how decimal positional notation works, and how numbers are compared, decomposed, and estimated.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Natural sandardyñ mölşerdı qalai bıldıretının, tsifrdyñ orny mänın qalai özgertetının jäne sandardy salystyru, ornalastyru, şamalau joldaryn tüsın.

#### Sandardy salystyru

Skills: 5

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/comparison/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Order relations between quantities and numerical representations, including comparison symbols and sorting numbers.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Mölşer men sandardy salystyryp, qaisysy ülken, kışı ne teñ ekenın anyqta jäne rette.

##### Salystyru tañbalary <, > jäne =

[comparisonSymbols.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/comparison/comparisonSymbols.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The symbols <, >, and = respectively express less than, greater than, and equality. Operand order determines inequality direction; swapping distinct numbers requires reversing the comparison sign.

**User-friendly description (kk):** <, > jäne = tañbalarymen kışı, ülken, teñ ekenın körset. Ekı türlı sannyñ ornyn auystyrsañ, teñsızdık tañbasynyñ bağyty özgeredı.

##### Köp, az nemese teñ mölşerler

[moreLessEqual.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/comparison/moreLessEqual.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Order relations between quantities depend on set cardinalities, not the size, area, or mass of the objects. Compare by one-to-one matching or by the numbers corresponding to the sets.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Zattardy bır-bırden säikestendır nemese sana: qai jiynda köp, az, teñ ekenın tap. Irı zattar sany köbırek degendı bıldırmeidı.

##### Ekı tañbaly sandardy salystyru jäne retteu

[order100.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/comparison/order100.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare the most significant decimal place first and move to the next place only when values match. For two-digit numbers the tens place takes precedence over the ones.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı tañbaly sandardy aldymen ondyğymen, ol teñ bolsa bırlıgımen salystyryp, rette.

##### Üş tañbaly sandardy salystyru jäne retteu

[order1000.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/comparison/order1000.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare three-digit decimal numerals from hundreds through tens to ones; the first unequal place determines their order. Lower-place zeros cannot outweigh a larger higher-place digit.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Üş tañbaly sandardy jüzdık, ondyq, bırlık boiynşa salystyr. Bırınşı aiyrmaşylyğy ülkenın anyqtaidy.

##### 0-den 20-ğa deiıngı sandardy retteu

[order20.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/comparison/order20.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Ordering numbers relies on the order relation: each next value in a nondecreasing sequence is no smaller, and in a nonincreasing sequence no greater. Equal repeated values do not break non-strict order.

**User-friendly description (kk):** 0-den 20-ğa deiıngı sandardy ösu ne kemu retımen ornalastyr. Bırdei sandar qaitalana alady.

#### Sandardy juyqtap bağalau

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/estimation/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Approximate numerical values and quantities, rounding, and matching estimation precision to the magnitude of the actual quantity.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Mölşer men mändı oryndy şamalap bağala jäne sandardy qajettı däldıkke deiın döñgelekte.

##### Mölşerdı bağalau jäne tekseru

[estimateQuantity.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/estimation/estimateQuantity.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Cardinality estimation produces an approximate count without first enumerating every object, using grouping or extrapolation from part of a set. An exact count independently checks the estimate.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Zattardyñ sanyn toptar ne şağyn bölık arqyly şamalap, keiın naqty sanap tekser.

##### Eñ jaqyn jüzdıkke deiın döñgelekteu

[roundToHundred.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/estimation/roundToHundred.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Rounding to the nearest hundred replaces a value with the closest multiple of one hundred. Rounding error is the difference between exact and rounded values; equidistant cases need an explicit rounding rule.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Jaqyn jüzdık eselıgın tauyp, naqty männen aiyrmasyn tüsın. Däl ortasynda arnaiy ereje qajet.

##### Eñ jaqyn ondyqqa deiın döñgelekteu

[roundToTen.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/estimation/roundToTen.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Rounding to the nearest ten replaces a value with the closest multiple of ten, comparing distances to neighboring tens. An exact halfway case needs an agreed tie-breaking convention.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı körşıles ondyq eselıgıne deiıngı qaşyqtyqty salystyryp, jaqynyn tañda. Däl ortasynda döñgelekteu erejesı kerek.

#### Sandardy jazu

Skills: 4

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/notation/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Digits as signs in the decimal system and the correspondence between spoken number names, written notation, and quantities for one-, two-, and three-digit numbers.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandardyñ aityluyn, tsifrmen jazyluyn jäne bıldıretın mölşerın bailanystyr, nöl men köptañbaly sandardy qosa.

##### 0–9 tsifrlary jäne tsifr men sannyñ aiyrmaşylyğy

[digits09.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/notation/digits09.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A digit is a symbol in decimal notation, whereas a number is a mathematical value expressible using one or more digits or another representation. Distinguish the written sign from quantity or numerical value.

**User-friendly description (kk):** 0-den 9-ğa deiıngı tsifrlar — jazu tañbalary, al san — olar bıldıretın män. Bır san bırneşe tsifrmen jazyluy mümkın.

##### 100-ge deiıngı sandardy oqu jäne jazu

[readWrite100.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/notation/readWrite100.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A two-digit decimal numeral represents tens and ones according to their positions. Reading, writing, and converting between spoken and written forms must preserve the same numerical value.

**User-friendly description (kk):** 100-ge deiıngı sandardy oqyp, jaz; ondyq pen bırlık ornynyñ mänın tüsın.

##### Üş tañbaly sandardy oqu jäne jazu

[readWrite1000.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/notation/readWrite1000.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A three-digit numeral encodes hundreds, tens, and ones. An internal zero indicates the absence of units at that place while retaining the places of following digits and the number's value.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Üş tañbaly sandardy jüzdık, ondyq, bırlık arqyly oqyp, jaz. Nöl bos razriadty körsetıp, basqa tsifrlardyñ ornyn saqtaidy.

##### 0–20 sandaryn oqu, jazu jäne mölşermen säikestendıru

[readWrite20.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/notation/readWrite20.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Associate a number's spoken name, its positional numeral, and its representation as a quantity with the same value. Zero also has a numeral and a cardinal meaning; a number is distinct from its representations.

**User-friendly description (kk):** 0-den 20-ğa deiıngı sandardy atauymen, jazyluymen jäne mölşerımen säikestendır. Nöl eş zat joq ekenın bıldıredı.

#### San tüzuı

Skills: 4

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/numberLine/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Numbers as points on an ordered scale with equal intervals; location, adjacency, and distance depend on the scale used.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandardy bırkelkı aralyqtary bar tüzude ornalastyr da, ornymen olardyñ retın, qaşyqtyğyn tüsın.

##### Aldyñğy, kelesı jäne aralyq sandar

[beforeAfterBetween.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/numberLine/beforeAfterBetween.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Where predecessor and successor exist in the relevant set, they differ from a natural number by one. Intermediate numbers are defined by numerical order and can be represented on a number line.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sannyñ däl aldynda ne artynda tūrğan sandy jäne ekı sannyñ arasyndağy sandardy tap.

##### San tüzuındegı bütın sandar arasyndağy qaşyqtyq

[distanceOnLine.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/numberLine/distanceOnLine.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distance between integer coordinates is the nonnegative absolute difference, independent of direction. On the number line it equals the number of unit intervals between them.

**User-friendly description (kk):** San tüzuındegı ekı bütın san nüktesınıñ arasyndağy bırlık kesındılerdı sana. Qaşyqtyq ekı bağytta bırdei.

##### 1000-ğa deiıngı sandar masştabtalğan san tüzuınde

[numberLine1000.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/numberLine/numberLine1000.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A point's location on a number line depends on its coordinate, origin, and unit length. Equal numeric changes require equal distances on a uniform scale; arbitrary spacing distorts the model.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bastapqy nüktesı men masştaby arqyly san tüzuınen 1000-ğa deiıngı sandardy tap. Bırdei sandyq qadamğa bırdei araqaşyqtyq säikes keledı.

##### 20-ğa deiıngı sandar san tüzuınde

[numberLine20.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/numberLine/numberLine20.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A number line orders numbers by coordinate; equal numerical increments occupy equal lengths on its scale. The predecessor and successor lie one unit interval to the left and right.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bırdei aralyqty san tüzuınen 20-ğa deiıngı sandardy tap. Bırlıkke jyljudyñ ūzyndyğy ärqaşan teñ.

#### Razriadtyq män

Skills: 11

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/placeValue/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The decimal structure of numbers, place values, exchanges between ones, tens, and hundreds, and equivalent decompositions of the same quantity.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tsifrdyñ orny onyñ mänın qalai özgertetının jäne bırlık, ondyq, jüzdıktı sandy özgertpei qalai toptastyruğa bolatynyn tüsın.

##### Tsifrdyñ razriadqa bailanysty mänı

[digitPlaceValue.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/placeValue/digitPlaceValue.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A digit's value depends on its position: the two digits 2 in 232 represent 200 and 2. Place value is distinct from the digit's graphic form.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tsifrdyñ orny mänın anyqtaidy: 232 sanyndağy ekı 2 sany 200 jäne 2-nı bıldıredı.

##### Sannyñ jıktelgen türı

[expandedForm.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/placeValue/expandedForm.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Standard expanded form expresses a number as the sum of its nonzero place values, and recombining the terms restores the number. This is a positional representation of the same value, not a different number.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandy razriadtyq qosylğyştarğa jıktep, qaita qūrastyr: 243 = 200 + 40 + 3.

##### Sandy ärtürlı täsılmen jıkteu

[flexiblePartition.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/placeValue/flexiblePartition.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A single number admits several equivalent additive decompositions, including non-place-value partitions. These rely on the associative property of addition and distinguish a value from a particular written representation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır sandy ärtürlı qosyndylarmen jazuğa bolady: 146 = 100 + 40 + 6 nemese 130 + 16.

##### Üş tañbaly sandardağy jüzdıkter, ondyqtar jäne bırlıkter

[hundredsTensOnes.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/placeValue/hundredsTensOnes.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A three-digit number has a unique standard decimal decomposition into hundreds, tens, and ones. Its digits provide coefficients of the corresponding place values; a zero indicates no units of that place.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Üş tañbaly sanda jüzdık, ondyq, bırlıktı tany, tıptı bır razriadta nöl bolsa da.

##### On ondyq bır jüzdıktı qūraidy

[makeHundred.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/placeValue/makeHundred.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Ten tens are equivalent to one hundred, or one hundred ones. This relation enables crossing the hundred boundary and understanding positional decimal notation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** On ondyq bır jüzdıkke teñ, jüz bırlık te solai. Toptau özgeredı, mölşerı özgermeidı.

##### On bırlıktı toptastyru jäne qaita jıkteu

[makeTen.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/placeValue/makeTen.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Ten units of a given place are equivalent to one unit of the next higher place. Regrouping and ungrouping preserve the number's value and underpin decimal notation and carrying.

**User-friendly description (kk):** On bırlıktı bır ondyqqa bırıktır nemese bır ondyqty qaita on bırlıkke böl. Mölşer özgermeidı.

##### Sannyñ ärtürlı körsetılımderın säikestendıru

[multipleRepresentations.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/placeValue/multipleRepresentations.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A positional numeral, a set of place-value blocks, a point on a number line, and the cardinality of a finite set can represent the same natural number. Converting among these preserves value rather than appearance.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır sandy tsifrmen jazyluynan, sanau tekşelerınen, san tüzuındegı nükteden nemese zattar jiynynan tany.

##### Razriadtar arasynda qaita toptastyru

[regroupPlaceValues.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/placeValue/regroupPlaceValues.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Equivalent place-value exchanges work in both directions: one hundred equals ten tens and one ten equals ten ones. The total value is preserved across different representations.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır jüzdıktı on ondyqqa nemese bır ondyqty on bırlıkke auystyr jäne kerı jasa. Jalpy män özgermeidı.

##### Ekı tañbaly sandardağy ondyqtar men bırlıkter

[tensOnes.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/placeValue/tensOnes.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Express a two-digit number as a multiple of ten plus its remaining ones without changing the value. The numeral, place-value blocks, and addition expression are equivalent representations of one number.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı tañbaly sandy ondyq pen bırlıkten qūrastyr nemese jıkte: 47 = 40 + 7.

##### Sandağy tolyq ondyqtar men jüzdıkterdıñ sany

[totalTensInNumber.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/placeValue/totalTensInNumber.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish the total number of complete units of a place value from the digit in that place: 348 contains 34 complete tens, although its tens digit is 4. Smaller-place remainders must be counted separately.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Sandağy barlyq tolyq ondyq pen jüzdıktı tap, tek sol razriadtyñ tsifryn emes. 348-de 34 tolyq ondyq bar.

##### Nöldıñ razriad ornyn belgıleu qyzmetı

[zeroPlaceholder.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/numeration/placeValue/zeroPlaceholder.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Zero in positional notation can signify no units at a particular place while preserving the place values of neighboring digits. Omitting that position may produce a different number.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Nöl bos razriadty saqtaidy: 305 sanynda ondyq joq, sondyqtan 305 pen 35 ärtürlı.

### Yqtimaldyq

Groups: 2 · Skills: 4

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/probability/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Possible outcomes of random experiments, events and their probabilities, comparisons of chance, independence or dependence of outcomes, and random variability in repeated observations.

#### Kezdeisoq oqiğalar

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/probability/events/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Events as subsets of outcomes of a random experiment, identifying possible and impossible occurrences, and comparing chances under specified conditions. Mathematical probability is not restricted to qualitative estimates.

##### Aqiqat jäne mümkın emes oqiğalardy ajyratu

[certainImpossible.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/probability/events/certainImpossible.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** For a specified random experiment, a certain event includes every possible outcome and an impossible event includes none. Other possible events can have different probabilities; possibility does not imply a 50% chance.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Berılgen kezdeisoq täjıribede qandai oqiğalar mındettı türde bolatynyn jäne qandailary mümkın emes ekenın ajyrata alasyñ. Oqiğanyñ mümkın boluy onyñ yqtimaldyğy 50% degen söz emes.

##### Kündelıktı oqiğalardyñ yqtimaldyğyn salystyru

[likelihoodLanguage.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/probability/events/likelihoodLanguage.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Probability describes the chance of an event under specified conditions, not merely whether it is possible. Comparisons require considering outcomes, their likelihoods, and the experimental conditions without assuming outcomes are equally likely.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Berılgen jağdaida kündelıktı oqiğalardyñ qaisysy yqtimalyraq ne yqtimaldyğy tömen ekenın salystyra alasyñ, barlyq nätijenıñ yqtimaldyğy teñ dep eseptemei.

##### Qarapaiym kezdeisoq täjıribenıñ mümkın nätijelerın tızu

[listOutcomes.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/probability/events/listOutcomes.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The sample space follows from a precisely specified random experiment. Listed elementary outcomes must be mutually exclusive and exhaustive at the chosen level of description; none may be added or omitted to favor a conclusion.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qarapaiym kezdeisoq täjıribenıñ barlyq mümkın nätijesın eşqaisyn qaldyrmai jäne ekı ret sanamai tıze alasyñ.

#### Kezdeisoq täjıribeler

Skills: 1

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/probability/experiments/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Variation in observed outcome frequencies across repeated series of random trials even when their conditions remain the same.

##### Qaitalanğan kezdeisoq täjıribelerdıñ nätijelerın salystyru

[experimentVariation.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/probability/experiments/experimentVariation.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Repetitions of a random experiment under identical conditions can yield different outcome frequencies across finite runs. This natural sampling variation must be distinguished from changes to the experiment's rules, conditions, or probabilities.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qaitalanğan kezdeisoq täjıribelerdıñ nätijelerın salystyryp, erejeler men yqtimaldyqtar özgermese de nätijelerdıñ kezdesu jiılıgı ärtürlı bolatynyn tüsıne alasyñ.

### Esepterdı şeşu

Groups: 7 · Skills: 23

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Translating real-life situations into mathematical models, selecting operations, planning multi-step solutions, and checking whether answers make sense.

#### Salystyru esepterı

Skills: 4

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/comparisons/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguishing additive comparison ('how many more or fewer') from multiplicative comparison ('how many times as many') and from problems describing a change in a quantity.

##### Aiyrmalyq salystyru esepterın şyğaru

[additiveComparison.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/comparisons/additiveComparison.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Additive comparison determines the nonnegative difference between quantities expressed in compatible units. Asking 'how many more or fewer' is not the multiplicative question 'how many times as many', which requires a different operation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı şamanyñ aiyrmasyn tauyp, bıreuı ekınşısınen qanşağa artyq ne kem ekenın anyqtai alasyñ; neşe ese ekenın emes.

##### Berılgen ese arttyru nemese kemıtu

[increaseDecreaseFactor.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/comparisons/increaseDecreaseFactor.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplicative change is modeled by multiplying by a positive factor or using the corresponding inverse operation. 'Increase by a factor of k' differs from 'increase by k units', and the result must be meaningful in context.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Şamany berılgen eselık koeffitsient boiynşa arttyryp ne kemıtıp, köbeitu-böludıñ tūraqty san qosu-azaitudan aiyrmasyn tüsıne alasyñ.

##### Berılgen sanğa arttyru nemese kemıtu

[increaseDecreaseNumber.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/comparisons/increaseDecreaseNumber.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Changing a quantity additively by a specified amount is represented by addition or subtraction according to the direction of change. An absolute increase must be distinguished from a multiplicative 'times as much' change.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Qosu nemese azaitu arqyly şamany berılgen sanğa arttyryp ne kemıte alasyñ, ony eselık özgerıspen şatastyrmaisyñ.

##### Eselık salystyru esepterın şyğaru

[multiplicativeComparison.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/comparisons/multiplicativeComparison.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplicative comparison finds the ratio between two positive quantities of the same dimension, not their difference. 'How many times as much' expresses a scale factor rather than an additive comparison.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı oñ şamanyñ qatynasyn paidalanyp, bıreuı ekınşısınen neşe ese ekenın taba alasyñ; aiyrmasyn emes.

#### Esep şarttaryn taldau

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/conditions/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Separating the question, known data, and implicit assumptions in a word problem before choosing an arithmetic operation.

##### Artyq mälımetterdı anyqtau

[findExtraneousData.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/conditions/findExtraneousData.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Extraneous information does not affect computing or justifying the answer to the specific question asked. The same detail can become relevant if the unknown changes, so mathematical relationships must be checked rather than merely deleting text.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Mätındı eseptıñ naqty sūrağyna jauap beru üşın qandai aqparat qajet emes ekenın anyqtap, jauapqa äser etetın derekterdı saqtai alasyñ.

##### Jetıspeitın mälımetterdı anyqtau

[findMissingData.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/conditions/findMissingData.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A problem has insufficient data when its stated conditions permit different answers to the same question. The missing quantity, relationship, or constraint needed for a unique answer must be identified rather than replaced with an arbitrary assumption.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Mätındı esepte bır ğana naqty jauap tabuğa derek jetpeitının baiqap, qandai şama nemese bailanys jetıspeitının tüsındıre alasyñ.

##### Belgılı jäne belgısız şamalardy anyqtau

[identifyKnownUnknown.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/conditions/identifyKnownUnknown.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Analyzing a word problem separates given quantities and their relationships from the unknown and the question to be answered. Narrative details need not be mathematical data, and keywords alone do not determine the solution method.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Mätındı esepten berılgen derekterdı, şamalardy, olardyñ bailanysyn jäne nenı tabu keregın anyqtai alasyñ, oqiğadağy artyq bölşekterge alañdamai.

#### Toptastyru esepterı

Skills: 2

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/groups/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Situations involving equal groups and independent selections from two sets, distinguishing multiplication from counting combinations.

##### Ekı jiynnyñ kombinatsiialaryn sanau

[correspondenceCombinations.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/groups/correspondenceCombinations.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Choosing one element independently from each of two finite sets produces a number of ordered pairs equal to the product of their sizes. The enumeration must be complete and free of duplicates; using a table, tree, or list does not change the count.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı jiynnan bır-bır element tañdau arqyly jasalatyn barlyq mümkın jūpty eşqaisyn qaldyrmai ne qaitalamai sanai alasyñ.

##### Teñ toptarğa arnalğan esepterdı şyğaru

[equalGroups.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/groups/equalGroups.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The total number of objects in equal groups is the number of groups multiplied by the size of each group. Any unknown one of the three related quantities can be obtained from the other two by the appropriate inverse operation when division is valid.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Teñ toptar turaly esepterdı top sany, är toptağy element sany jäne jalpy sannyñ bailanysyn köbeitu ne bölu arqyly şyğara alasyñ.

#### Esep modelderı

Skills: 4

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/models/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relationships between a concrete situation, drawing, schematic model, and numerical expression representing the required operation.

##### Qosu nemese azaitu amalyn tañdau

[chooseOperationAddSub.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/models/chooseOperationAddSub.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The choice between addition and subtraction depends on the relationship between known and unknown quantities: combining, changing, comparing, or finding a part. The same wording in different problems does not always imply the same operation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Belgılı jäne belgısız şamalardyñ bailanysyn tüsınıp, tek tırek sözderge süienbei qosu ne azaitudy tañdai alasyñ.

##### Köbeitu nemese bölu amalyn tañdau

[chooseOperationMulDiv.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/models/chooseOperationMulDiv.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Multiplication relates the number of equal groups, the size of each group, and their total; division finds an unknown component from the other two. The structure of equal groups determines the operation rather than a particular word in the problem.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Teñ toptardyñ sany, är toptağy elementter sany jäne jalpy sanyna qarap köbeitu ne böludı tañdai alasyñ.

##### Model boiynşa mätındık esep qūrastyru

[createProblem.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/models/createProblem.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A constructed word problem must match the given mathematical model in its quantities, operations, known information, and unknowns. One expression can support several suitable story contexts, but each must preserve the underlying mathematical structure.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Suretke, kestege nemese örnekke sai mätındı esep qūrastyryp, şamalar men matematikalyq bailanystardy saqtai alasyñ.

##### Bır amaldyq eseptı modeldeu

[oneStepModel.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/models/oneStepModel.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A mathematical model must preserve the original problem's quantities, unknown, and relationships, regardless of whether it is a drawing, diagram, or expression. Using the correct numbers to represent a different relationship does not yield a valid model.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır amalmen şyğarylatyn mätındı eseptı belgılı derekter men ızdeletın şamany dūrys körsetetın suret, syzba nemese örnekpen beinelei alasyñ.

#### Bölık pen bütınge arnalğan esepter

Skills: 2

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/parts/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relationships between a whole and its parts in contextual problems, including unit fractional parts.

##### Şamanyñ bırlık bölşegın tabu

[fractionsContext.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/parts/fractionsContext.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A unit fraction 1/n of a nonnegative quantity is obtained by dividing the whole into n equal parts for positive n. The situation must identify the chosen unit whole, and the selected part must be relative to that same whole.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bütındı teñ bölıkterge bölıp, onyñ bırlık bölşegın, mysaly törtten bırın, taba alasyñ jäne bölşek qai bütınge qatysty ekenın anyqtai alasyñ.

##### Bölık pen bütınge arnalğan esepterdı şyğaru

[partWholeAddsub.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/parts/partWholeAddsub.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** When a whole consists of parts of 7 and 5, adding the parts reconstructs the whole; when the whole and one part are known, the other part is determined by subtraction.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bütın men bölıkter turaly esepterdı şyğara alasyñ: belgılı bölıkterdı qosyp bütındı nemese bütınnen belgılı bölıktı azaityp jetıspeitın bölıktı tabasyñ.

#### Şeşımdı josparlau

Skills: 5

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/planning/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Constructing and justifying a sequence of solution steps, checking units and answers, and considering alternative methods.

##### Kerı esepterdı qūrastyru

[constructInverseProblem.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/planning/constructInverseProblem.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Constructing an inverse word problem changes the roles of given and unknown quantities while preserving the mathematical relationship and allowing the original situation to be recovered. The competency is formulating a valid new situation and question; subsequently solving it assesses existing arithmetic and problem-solving skills, not a required part of this skill.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Belgılı jäne ızdeletın şamalardyñ oryndaryn auystyryp, bastapqy matematikalyq bailanysty saqtai otyryp kerı mätındı esep qūrastyra alasyñ.

##### Jauap bırlıkterı men qisyndylyğyn tekseru

[explainAnswerUnits.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/planning/explainAnswerUnits.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A word-problem answer must name the requested quantity in consistent units and satisfy the constraints of its mathematical or real-world context. A bare number without a unit or a plausibility check may fail to answer the question.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tek san jazbai, jauapty dūrys ölşem bırlıgımen berıp, onyñ jağdaiğa sai mağynaly ekenın teksere alasyñ.

##### Şeşu täsılderın salystyru

[multipleSolutionStrategies.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/planning/multipleSolutionStrategies.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Different algorithms or models can reach the same correct answer. Comparing strategies requires mathematical validity, justification of each step, computational complexity, and the conditions under which each method applies.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Eseptı şeşudıñ ekı dūrys täsılın salystyryp, ärqaisysy qaşan jaraitynyn jäne qaisysy tiımdı ekenın tüsındıre alasyñ.

##### Üş amaldyq eseptı şyğaru

[threeStepPlan.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/planning/threeStepPlan.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A three-step solution successively determines intermediate results required to find the primary unknown. Every operation must follow from the problem's conditions and each result must retain its contextual meaning.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Özara bailanysty üş qadamdyq eseptı aralyq nätijeler arqyly şyğaryp, mağynaly soñğy jauapqa jete alasyñ.

##### Ekı amaldyq eseptıñ şeşu josparyn qūru

[twoStepPlan.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/planning/twoStepPlan.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A two-step solution includes an intermediate quantity that must be found before the final answer. The order of steps follows dependencies between the given and unknown quantities, not simply the written order of operation signs.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ekı qadamdyq şeşımdı josparlap, aldymen qandai aralyq şamany tabu keregın jäne äreketter retınıñ sebebın tüsındıre alasyñ.

#### Şamalarğa arnalğan esepter

Skills: 3

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/quantities/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Practical relationships among work rate, time, price, quantity, mass, capacity, and length.

##### Ölşeu esepterın modeldeu

[measurementContext.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/quantities/measurementContext.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Modeling a word problem involving measured quantities requires identifying the physical quantity, its unit, and relationships between known and unknown values. Length, mass, capacity, and time are possible contexts rather than mandatory separate parts of this single skill; consistent units and dimensions determine model validity.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Ūzyndyq, massa, syiymdylyq, uaqyt ne basqa ölşenetın şama turaly mätındı eseptı ölşem bırlıkterın säikestendırıp matematikalyq bailanysqa ainaldyra alasyñ.

##### Bağa, san jäne qūn arasyndağy bailanys

[priceQuantityCost.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/quantities/priceQuantityCost.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** When unit price is constant, total cost is price multiplied by quantity. The model must distinguish price per unit from the monetary total, and recognize that different price-and-quantity pairs can give the same total.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır zattyñ bağasy, zat sany jäne jalpy qūn arasyndağy bailanysty tüsıne alasyñ: bırlık bağa tūraqty bolsa, bağa men sannyñ köbeitındısı jalpy qūn bolady.

##### Önımdılık, uaqyt jäne jūmys kölemı arasyndağy bailanys

[workRateTime.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/problemSolving/quantities/workRateTime.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** At a constant work rate, the amount of completed work equals rate multiplied by elapsed time. Units must be consistent, and the formula does not directly model varying rates without an additional assumption or model.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Tūraqty jūmys önımdılıgı, ötken uaqyt jäne oryndalğan jūmys arasyndağy bailanysty tüsıne alasyñ: önımdılık özgermese, önımdılık × uaqyt = jūmys kölemı.

### Paiymdau

Groups: 4 · Skills: 9

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/reasoning/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Justifying mathematical statements, finding counterexamples, drawing logical conclusions, checking solutions, and translating between representations.

#### Matematikalyq däleldeu

Skills: 5

[index.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/reasoning/argumentation/index.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Justifying conclusions from mathematical conditions, evaluating universal statements, and explaining the selected solution method.

##### Zattar men sandardy ereje boiynşa jıkteu jäne tañdaudy negızdeu

[classifyAndJustify.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/reasoning/argumentation/classifyAndJustify.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Only numbers divisible by three may belong to a specified group; membership must be justified by the mathematical classification rule, not by superficial similarities of notation.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Zattardy nemese sandardy anyq ereje boiynşa toptastyryp, är elementtıñ topqa nelıkten kıretının ne kırmeitının tüsındıre alasyñ.

##### Jeke mysal men jalpy erejenı ajyratu

[distinguishExampleRule.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/reasoning/argumentation/distinguishExampleRule.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A confirming instance does not establish a universal mathematical proposition. A general rule requires justification across the entire specified class, while one valid counterexample refutes it.

**User-friendly description (kk):** Bır mysaldy barlyq jağdaida oryndaluy tiıs jalpy erejeden ajyrata alasyñ. Säikes keletın bır mysal jalpy erejenı däleldemeidı.

##### Berılgen şarttar men paiymdaudan qorytyndy şyğaru

[drawConclusion.ts](../../../content/math/data/skills/reasoning/argumentation/drawConclusion.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A logical conclusion must follow from established premises and prior statements through valid inference rules. Necessary consequences must be distinguished from plausible guesses and conclusions based on insufficient conditions.
